areas.purpose: Turn washed product hydrate (gibbsite, Al(OH)3) into smelter-grade alumina (SGA). Two identical gas suspension calciner trains with holding vessels (GSC-HV) dry, dehydrate (calcine) and cool it. The area also holds a product-hydrate slurry buffer so that a calciner outage does not force an immediate cut in refinery output. Calcination sets product LOI, BET surface area and alpha-alumina content. It cannot remove soda or fix weak particles: Na2O and particle size come from precipitation and hydrate washing (A13/A14). This is the refinery's largest single fuel user and CO2 source.
areas.process_description:
TECHNOLOGY CHOICE: The reference plant uses the FLSmidth-type Gas Suspension Calciner with Holding Vessel (GSC-HV), 2 trains x 3,500 t/d nameplate. The alternative is the Metso Outotec (ex-Lurgi) Circulating Fluid Bed (CFB) calciner. Both are proven at about 3,000-4,500 t/d per unit with similar fuel use (about 2.8-3.1 GJ/t). GSC was chosen for three reasons. (a) Its stages suit the training curriculum: venturi flash dryer, 2 preheater cyclone stages, stationary furnace, holding vessel, 4 cooling-cyclone stages, fluid bed cooler and ESP. (b) The whole gas path runs under suction from one ID fan, so there are no high-pressure primary-air blowers and dust cannot leak outward. (c) It holds little material, so it starts and stops quickly. CFB differences are noted under 'alternatives'.
STEP 0 - Hydrate buffer (15-TK-001/002): Normally, product hydrate slurry from the A13 product classification goes straight to the A14 product filters. When one calciner is down (refractory relines take about 2-3 weeks per unit per year, plus trips), the shortfall is about 3,500 t/d of dry hydrate. That slurry (about 40-50 wt% solids in spent liquor) is diverted to two agitated storage tanks, which hold about 4-5 days of the shortfall. Afterwards it is pumped back to the product filters at a controlled rate while both calciners run at up to about 110-121 % of average demand. Outages longer than the buffer need a planned cut in refinery rate.
STEP 1 - Feed: Washed hydrate filter cake from the A14 product hydrate filters falls by chute or short belt into each train's calciner feed bin. The cake is at 6-10 % free moisture and 50-80 degC, with about 0.20-0.30 % Na2O on a dry hydrate basis and d50 about 80-100 um. Twin variable-speed screw feeders meter it into the venturi flash dryer.
STEP 2 - Drying (stage A01/P01): Gas leaving preheater cyclone P02 at about 350-420 degC enters through a venturi throat at the bottom of the dryer riser. It lifts the hydrate and the free moisture flashes off in about 1-2 s. Two dryer cyclones (P01) separate the dried hydrate at about 140-170 degC. The gas (about 140-170 degC, about 45-55 vol% H2O) goes to the ESP, then the ID fan, then the stack.
STEP 3 - Preheating and partial dehydration (P02): P01 solids are injected into the riser duct that carries furnace gas (about 950-1050 degC) from the P04 cyclones. In about a second they reach about 320-400 degC and start to dehydrate: 2 Al(OH)3 -> Al2O3 + 3 H2O(g). The reaction absorbs about +205 kJ/mol, or about 2.0 GJ/t Al2O3 including vaporising the water (thermochemical calculation from standard heats of formation). The heat in the furnace gas limits how far it goes in P02. A heat balance gives roughly 35-60 % of the bound water released here, with solids LOI falling from 34.6 % to roughly 15-25 % (engineering estimate). Furnace and HV complete the rest. Fine particles heated fast go gibbsite -> chi-alumina, while coarse particles in humid gas partly go to boehmite (AlOOH) first.
STEP 4 - Calcination (P04 furnace): The partly dehydrated solids enter the lower cone of the refractory-lined stationary furnace. Combustion air from cooling cyclone C01 arrives at about 650-800 degC. Natural gas is injected through a ring of burners in the cone and burns with the solids in suspension. Gas and solids leave the top at about 950-1050 degC, a set point that controls LOI and BET, with 2-4 % excess O2. Gas residence time in the furnace is only about 1-3 s. The furnace separation cyclones (P04) split the solids from the gas, which goes on to P02 (step 3).
STEP 5 - Holding vessel (HV): Solids from P04 drop into an air-fluidised, refractory-lined holding vessel. They stay about 10-30 min (engineering estimate) at about 920-1000 degC, which finishes the last hydroxyl removal. With the HV the furnace can run about 50-100 degC cooler than a GSC without one for the same LOI (vendor claim). That gives higher BET, lower alpha-alumina and lower fuel use. HV off-air returns to the furnace.
STEP 6 - Suspension cooling (C01-C04): Hot alumina passes counter-current through 4 cooling-cyclone stages. The ID fan draws ambient air, plus the FBC exhaust air, in at the C04 riser. The air takes up heat stage by stage and becomes the furnace combustion air. Alumina cools from about 950-1000 degC to about 180-280 degC, and the air heats from about 30-60 degC to about 650-800 degC. In this service the air carries about 15-20 % more heat per degree than the alumina (about 125,000-145,000 Nm3/h of air vs 146 t/h of alumina per train). An ideal 4-stage balance therefore gives at most about 730 degC air and about 160 degC alumina, and real stages fall a little short of that (engineering estimate).
STEP 7 - Fluid bed cooler (FBC): Alumina from C04 enters a multi-compartment air-fluidised bed. Water-cooled tube bundles immersed in the bed bring it to about 70-90 degC (duty about 5-8 MW per train). The heat goes through plate heat exchangers to make hot wash water for the hydrate filters, with a cooling tower as trim. Warm FBC exhaust air goes into the C04 air inlet so its heat is recovered.
STEP 8 - Product: The FBC overflows into airslides feeding the dense-phase conveyors to the product silos (A16). An auto-sampler takes samples for LOI, MOI, BET, alpha, PSD, Na2O and impurities and makes hourly composites.
PHASE CHEMISTRY: Gibbsite goes to chi or boehmite, then gamma, delta and theta (the transition aluminas, BET 60-80 m2/g in SGA), and finally alpha (corundum). Alpha forms significantly only above about 1100-1200 degC and is held below about 10 % in SGA, because it dissolves slowly in cryolite and lowers HF scrubbing capacity at the smelter. Raising calcination temperature lowers LOI and BET and raises alpha. Holding solids longer at moderate temperature (the HV) lowers LOI and keeps BET high.
HIGH-TEMPERATURE (BOEHMITIC) PLANTS: they use the same calciner technology. The differences are upstream: digestion at 240-270 degC with flash/heat-recovery trains. Hydrate quality depends on precipitation practice, not on the digestion route.
GAS SIDE: the whole GSC gas path is under negative pressure, from about -0.5 kPa at the C04 air inlet to about -9 to -13 kPa at the ID fan inlet (engineering estimate). That covers 7 cyclone stages in series plus the venturi, furnace, ESP and ducts. The ESP outlet dust limit is 30-50 mg/Nm3 (typical licence, set by jurisdiction). The off-gas is very humid (dew point about 78-85 degC), so all ducts, the ESP and the stack must run well above about 120 degC.

streams.flow: ~240-250 t/h wet per train at nameplate (~223 t/h dry = 1.53 t dry hydrate/t Al2O3 x 146 t/h); plant ~395-410 t/h wet at 241 t/h Al2O3

equipment.name: Product hydrate slurry storage tanks (calciner-outage buffer) with agitators and reclaim pumps
equipment.function: Store product hydrate slurry while one calciner is down, then return it to the product filters, so that a calciner outage does not immediately cut refinery output.
equipment.qty_operating: 2 tanks (normally low level, filled during outages); 1 reclaim pump
equipment.type_selected: Vertical flat-bottom (or shallow-cone) carbon-steel tanks with top-entry hydrofoil agitators (precipitator-type), centrifugal slurry reclaim pumps
equipment.why_this_type: Many Bayer refineries keep hydrate storage ahead of calcination. Holding the hydrate as slurry in spent liquor uses the same tank and agitator design as precipitation, is easy to reclaim by pump, and needs no extra filtration step. A covered wet-cake shed with front-end loaders is the alternative, but it handles cake twice and makes dust and contamination risks worse.
key_dimensions: Working volume ~8,000-10,000 m3 each, e.g. ~22-24 m ID x ~24-26 m tall (engineering estimate)
Capacity ~15,000-17,000 t dry hydrate total (~1.18 m3 slurry per t hydrate at 50 wt%), ~4-5 days of the one-calciner shortfall (engineering estimate)
Agitator ~200-300 kW, 2-3 hydrofoil impellers on a ~25 m shaft (engineering estimate)
Reclaim pumps ~200-400 m3/h at ~30-40 m (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate (limited by spare calciner and filter capacity)

equipment.working_principle: While one calciner is down, a diverter on the product hydrate slurry line sends the surplus slurry into these tanks. The agitators keep the coarse hydrate (d50 about 90 um) suspended, and the tank level rises over the outage. The liquor is spent liquor, so the hydrate is stable and grows only slightly. When both calciners are back, the reclaim pumps return slurry to the A14 product filters at a controlled rate. Both calciners then run above the average rate (up to 3,500 t/d each) until the tanks are drawn down. Agitators must never stop with solids in the tank, because coarse hydrate settles fast and sets into a hard bed.
details_to_model: Two large cylindrical tanks with fixed roof and bridge-mounted top-entry agitator drives (motor, gearbox and support beam), roof walkway and handrails
Inlet nozzle with downcomer; side-outlet suction nozzles near the bottom with knife-gate isolation valves; overflow and drain nozzles; flushing liquor connections
Slurry pumps in a bunded pump bay with suction and discharge knife-gate valves, pressure gauges and flush connections
Radar level transmitter, agitator power/torque monitoring, bottom scour/sparge connections; external spiral stair, roof manhole, shell manways (2)
Concrete bund with sump pump; safety showers at stair base and pump bay
hazards_and_safety: Caustic spent liquor (~240 g/L as Na2CO3 at ~60 degC): burns and eye damage; face shield, gauntlets, safety showers
Confined-space entry only after draining, washing, isolation of the agitator (LOTO) and gas test
Agitator failure with a full tank: risk of sanded tank and overloaded drive on restart
common_problems: Hydrate settling and scaling on walls and impellers if the tank stands half-full for long periods
Pump wear and line plugging on reclaim
operating_tips_and_key_points: Keep the tanks near empty in normal operation so the full buffer is available
Agree the outage plan with precipitation: past ~4-5 days the refinery rate must be cut
instrumentation_and_control: Tank LT with high/high-high alarms; agitator current and torque trip
Reclaim FIC to A14 filter feed; slurry density meter
equipment.materials: Carbon steel tanks (caustic service below the NACE SP0403 SCC limit at <70 degC with PWHT of nozzles per the owner's caustic materials philosophy); hard-metal or rubber-lined pumps
sources: Common Bayer practice (hydrate storage ahead of calcination); review finding (mechanical)

equipment.name: Calciner hydrate feed bin
equipment.function: Buffers wet hydrate from the product filter so that pulses in cake discharge do not upset the steady calciner feed.
equipment.type_selected: Vertical cylindrical steel bin with steep conical (or wedge/transition) mass-flow hopper, load-cell mounted
equipment.why_this_type: Wet hydrate (6-10 % moisture) is cohesive and bridges. A steep, low-friction mass-flow hopper feeding twin screws gives first-in-first-out flow and a measurable inventory for feed control.
key_dimensions: Diameter ~6-8 m, cylinder ~6-8 m, cone ~5-7 m (engineering estimate)
Live capacity ~150-300 t (~0.6-1.2 h at 240 t/h) (engineering estimate)
Hopper half-angle ~15-25 deg from vertical, lined (engineering estimate, to be confirmed by Jenike flow-function testing)
equipment.working_principle: Filter cake falls into the bin from the filter discharge chute or belt. The bin sits on 3-4 load cells, so the control system always knows the inventory. Screw speed sets the calciner feed rate, which is checked against the rate the bin weight falls while filter feed is stopped. A steep, smooth cone gives mass flow: all the material moves together, with no dead zones where wet hydrate can cake and later collapse. The bin vents into the dryer inlet, which is under suction, so steam and dust stay inside the system.
details_to_model: Cylindrical shell with roof; top inlet chute from filter discharge with inspection door; vent nozzle (DN 300-500) ducted to dryer inlet
Cone lined with UHMWPE or 304/2B stainless wear plates fixed with countersunk bolts; 2 rectangular slot outlets at the cone bottom to the twin screw feeders
3-4 load cells on bracket lugs at a ring girder on structural steel at ~30-40 m level of the calciner tower
Radar level transmitter on the roof, high-high level switch, 2-3 air blasters or vibrator pads on the cone, poke/inspection ports with hinged covers
Roof manhole (DN 600) with handrail perimeter platform, ladder from tower floor
No thermal insulation normally; external stiffeners on cylinder
hazards_and_safety: Confined space; engulfment by collapsing hydrate bridges: never enter without isolation, permit and standby person, and clear bridging from above
Mildly caustic wet hydrate (residual soda) irritates skin and eyes
Isolate and depressurise air blasters before entry
common_problems: Rat-holing/bridging with high-moisture cake
Lumps from filter cloth failures blocking screws
operating_tips_and_key_points: Hydrate moisture above ~10 % lowers dryer exit temperature and upsets P01 flow: fix the filters first
Keep bin level steady; a bin running empty lets air bypass into the dryer and upsets the draft
instrumentation_and_control: Load cells WT
Radar LT, LSHH
Feed rate from screw speed SIC + loss-in-weight check
equipment.materials: Carbon steel shell, UHMWPE or stainless cone liner
sources: Jenike A.W., Storage and Flow of Solids, Bulletin 123 (hopper design method)
FLSmidth GSC vendor literature (feed system arrangement)

equipment.name: Hydrate feed screw feeders
equipment.function: Meter wet hydrate from the feed bin into the venturi flash dryer, with a plug of material sealing out the dryer suction.
equipment.qty_standby: 0 (each screw sized ~60-70 % of train feed so one can carry the train at reduced rate)
equipment.type_selected: Twin variable-speed screw feeders with plug-forming discharge section
equipment.why_this_type: Screws handle sticky cake and give a feed rate proportional to speed. A short shaftless or choke section forms a material seal against the dryer's suction.
key_dimensions: Screw diameter ~600-800 mm, length ~5-8 m (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: A rotating helical flight in a U-trough or tube pushes forward a fixed volume of hydrate per turn, so the feed rate is roughly proportional to speed. Near the outlet a tubular section keeps the screw full. That plug of hydrate seals the bin from the dryer suction. The screw discharges into a feed chute that enters the dryer riser just above the venturi throat.
details_to_model: Trough/tube casing with bolted inspection covers
Inlet flange to bin outlet, discharge chute with expansion bellows into the dryer riser
Helical-bevel gear motor on the drive end with coupling guard; end bearings with grease lines
Zero-speed sensor on the tail shaft (enclosed unit, no pull-cord)
Hard-faced wear-resistant flights (visible when cover removed)
hazards_and_safety: Moving machinery: never open inspection covers while running; lock out at MCC
Hot gas blow-back at dryer inlet if the plug is lost
common_problems: Flight wear and hydrate build-up on the shaft
Feed surges when the bin bridges
instrumentation_and_control: VFD speed control from calciner feed-rate controller
Motor current monitoring, zero-speed switch
equipment.materials: Carbon steel casing, hard-faced or AR400 flights
sources: CEMA 350 Screw Conveyors for Bulk Materials

equipment.name: Venturi flash dryer (stage A01) with dryer hot-gas generator
equipment.function: Flash-dries wet hydrate (removes free moisture) using waste heat in the gas from preheater cyclone P02. The dryer burner supplies heat for start-up and trim.
equipment.type_selected: Vertical abrasion-lined venturi riser dryer with side-mounted gas-fired hot-gas generator
equipment.why_this_type: The venturi gives the high velocity needed to break up and lift wet agglomerates. Suspension drying is fast and has no moving parts.
key_dimensions: Venturi throat ~2.2-2.8 m dia (~30-45 m/s at ~175 Am3/s gas from P02) (engineering estimate)
Riser ~3.5-4.5 m dia (~10-15 m/s), height ~15-25 m to P01 inlet ducts (engineering estimate)
Hot-gas generator ~3-4 m dia x 6-8 m long, rated ~10-25 MW (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate consistent with GSC literature
engineering estimate; must stay well above off-gas dew point ~78-85 degC
engineering estimate (evaporation + heating hydrate to ~150 degC)

equipment.working_principle: Hot gas speeds up through a converging-diverging venturi at the base of the riser. Wet hydrate drops in just above the throat. The turbulence breaks up lumps and the gas carries the particles upward. Heat moves very fast into the small particles, so the free water evaporates in about a second and the gas cools from about 400 degC to about 150 degC. Gas and dry hydrate leave the top of the riser for the P01 cyclones. During start-up and heat-up, before P02 gas is hot enough, or with very wet feed, the dryer burner adds hot flue gas at the inlet.
details_to_model: Vertical cylindrical riser rising from the venturi cone; bottom gas-inlet elbow from the P02 gas duct (large rectangular-to-round transition, ~3 m)
Feed chute entering at ~45 deg just above the throat, with flushing/inspection door
Riser top: bifurcated outlet ducts (2) to the two P01 cyclone tangential inlets
Hot-gas generator: horizontal refractory-lined burner chamber with burner front (gas train, flame scanner, combustion-air fan) joined to the inlet duct
Lining ~100-150 mm abrasion-resistant castable on anchors; external shell stiffening rings; thermocouples at inlet, throat and outlet; pressure taps at throat (venturi dP)
Inspection doors at 2-3 levels with platforms; metallic/fabric expansion joints on ducts; spring supports/hangers
hazards_and_safety: Hot surfaces (shell 80-150 degC). The system is under suction, but opening doors during an upset or positive pressure ejects hot dust
Burner: purge and flame supervision per NFPA 85/86 / EN 746-2
Steam and hot dust when clearing blockages
common_problems: Dryer 'choking' (wet feed collapses) when outlet temperature drops; build-up at the feed point
Erosion of throat lining
operating_tips_and_key_points: Watch dryer outlet temperature: it is the first warning of a change in feed moisture or feed rate
instrumentation_and_control: TT inlet/outlet; PDT across venturi
Dryer burner on BMS with UV/IR scanner
sources: FLSmidth GSC vendor literature (flash dryer stage)
Raahauge B.E. & Williams F.S. (eds), Smelter Grade Alumina from the Bayer Process, Springer 2022

equipment.name: Dryer (P01) separation cyclones
equipment.function: Separate dried hydrate from the cooled off-gas. The underflow goes to the P02 riser and the gas to the ESP.
equipment.type_selected: High-efficiency tangential (scroll) inlet cyclones with central vortex finder and pendulum flap valve on dip-leg
equipment.why_this_type: Standard suspension-preheater technology from the cement and alumina industries. High efficiency at P01 limits the dust load on the ESP.
key_dimensions: Gas per cyclone ~60-70 Am3/s at ~150 degC and ~-9 kPa (engineering estimate from off-gas balance)
Inlet duct ~3.2-3.8 m2 each (e.g. ~1.6 x 2.2 m scroll inlet) for ~18-20 m/s (CORRECTED per review; preheater practice 15-20 m/s)
Cylinder ID ~4.8-6.0 m (body up-flow ~3-4 m/s), overall height cylinder + cone ~15-20 m (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: suspension preheater practice (Duda, Cement Data Book: 15-20 m/s)

equipment.working_principle: Gas enters tangentially and spins down the cylinder and cone. Centrifugal force throws the particles to the wall, and they slide down into the dip-leg. The gas reverses at the bottom of the cone and leaves upward through the central vortex finder. Inlet velocity matters: below about 15 m/s the spin is too weak and efficiency falls sharply. A counterweighted pendulum flap in the dip-leg opens only under the weight of solids, which stops gas short-circuiting up the dip-leg and ruining separation.
details_to_model: Cylinder + cone shell with involute (scroll) rectangular inlet, taller than wide; vortex finder pipe projecting into the cylinder; top gas outlet duct to the common off-gas duct
Dip-leg with pendulum flap valve housing (external counterweight arm, limit switch), inspection doors above and below the flap
3-6 air blasters on the cone (tanks + discharge nozzles), poke holes with caps
Thin lining (gunite/abrasion castable ~50-75 mm) on this cold stage
Support lugs on the cyclone cylinder bearing on tower beams; platforms at inlet level and flap level
Thermocouple and pressure tap on the outlet duct; cone draft (pressure) tap for blockage detection
hazards_and_safety: Clearing cyclone blockages: hot dust can burst out of doors. Use remote lances, face shields and aluminised clothing, and never stand in line with a door
Confined-space entry only after cool-down, gas test, and isolation of air blasters and fan
common_problems: Cone build-up from condensation if outlet temperature is low
Flap valve sticking open (gas bypass) or shut (blockage)
instrumentation_and_control: Cone pressure (low-draft alarm signals blockage)
Flap position switch
sources: Duda W.H., Cement Data Book (cyclone inlet velocity practice)

equipment.name: Preheater (P02) cyclones and riser
equipment.function: Heat dried hydrate to ~320-400 degC with furnace gas, starting dehydration, and cool the gas before it goes to the dryer.
equipment.type_selected: Refractory-lined tangential cyclones with heat-resistant vortex finders and pendulum flaps
equipment.why_this_type: Gas-solid heat exchange in suspension (risers + cyclones) is close to counter-current overall and very efficient.
key_dimensions: Gas per cyclone ~85-95 Am3/s at ~380 degC (engineering estimate)
Inlet ~4.4-5.2 m2 inside lining (e.g. ~1.8 x 2.6 m) for ~18-20 m/s (CORRECTED per review)
Cylinder ID ~5.3-6.3 m inside lining, height ~16-22 m (engineering estimate)
Riser duct (from P04 gas outlets) ~3-4 m ID (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate from P02 heat balance (gas heat limits dehydration to ~35-60 % of bound water)

equipment.working_principle: Dried hydrate from P01 is injected into the hot riser duct carrying gas from the furnace cyclones. Fine particles in suspension heat up in a second or less. The hydrate starts to lose its 34.6 % theoretical combined water and turns into chi-alumina or boehmite. Because the dehydration absorbs a lot of heat, the furnace gas can supply only part of it, so roughly a third to a half of the bound water leaves here and the rest in the furnace and HV. The P02 cyclones separate the solids, which drop into the furnace cone, while the gas (now about 350-420 degC) goes on to the dryer.
details_to_model: As for P01 but with full refractory lining (~150-230 mm insulating + dense castable/brick)
Segmented vortex finder of heat-resistant cast steel hung from the roof (visible from roof hatch)
Pendulum flap on the dip-leg in a refractory-lined flap box, plus a splash box at the riser injection point
Riser-to-cyclone ducts with expansion joints; many TC and pressure points on ducts and cyclones
Shell IR-scanner coverage and painted temperature-indicating patches for hot spots
hazards_and_safety: Shell up to ~150-250 degC: personnel guards near walkways
Hot meal (300-400 degC) flows like a liquid if a blockage releases
common_problems: Refractory damage at the inlet scroll; loss of vortex finder segments
Build-up at riser injection point
instrumentation_and_control: TT gas outlet P02 (key profile reading)
Cone draft PT, flap position
equipment.materials: Carbon steel shell; refractory; heat-resistant cast steel (e.g., 25Cr-20Ni class) vortex finder
sources: Wefers K. & Misra C., Oxides and Hydroxides of Aluminum, Alcoa Technical Paper 19 (1987) (dehydration sequence)

equipment.name: Calciner furnace (P04) with main burners
equipment.function: Burn fuel in preheated air with the alumina in suspension, completing dehydration and raising the solids to calcination temperature (950-1050 degC).
equipment.type_selected: Stationary, refractory-lined, vertical cylindrical suspension furnace with conical bottom air inlet and ring of gas burners (fuel-oil lances optional)
equipment.why_this_type: Combustion in suspension with the material is very efficient. There is no moving kiln shell and the refractory area is small. Rotary kilns used ~4.5-5 GJ/t against ~3 GJ/t for stationary calciners.
key_dimensions: Shell ID inside lining ~6-7 m (~210-230 Am3/s at ~6-8 m/s); cylindrical height ~20-28 m plus bottom cone ~6-8 m (engineering estimate)
Refractory total ~250-350 mm (insulating brick/board + dense high-alumina castable/brick) (engineering estimate)
Burners: ~6-12 per furnace in 1-2 rings (engineering estimate)
Hot-air inlet duct from C01 ~2.5-3.5 m ID inside lining (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: GSC-HV practice (Raahauge & Williams 2022; vendor literature); 1050-1150 degC without holding vessel
engineering estimate from 4-stage cooler heat balance (CORRECTED from 750-900)

equipment.working_principle: Preheated air from cooling cyclone C01 rises into the furnace through the bottom cone at high velocity. Natural gas from the burner lances mixes with this hot air and burns. The partly dehydrated alumina from P02 is fed in at the cone, where it is lifted and heated quickly to the set temperature. The remaining bound water leaves here, and the solids are carried out of the top into the P04 cyclones. Fuel rate trims the temperature, which sets LOI, BET and alpha content. The cone shape spreads the air jet and gives back-mixing that evens out temperatures. Before ignition, the BMS runs a purge of at least 4-5 volume changes and lights the start-up burner.
details_to_model: Tall vertical cylinder in the central bay of the calciner tower; bottom cone with large vertical hot-air inlet duct from C01 (refractory-lined)
Material inlet chute(s) from P02 dip-legs entering the cone at 45-60 deg with splash plates

Burner ring: 6-12 gas lances arranged radially round the cone at a burner platform, each with manual isolation valve, automatic shut-off valve pair, flexible hose, flame-scanner sight tube and cooling/purge-air connection
Start-up burner (larger, with its own combustion-air fan) at the bottom; igniters
Top outlet: 1 or 2 large refractory-lined ducts curving to the P04 cyclones
Inspection/manway doors at 3-4 levels (refractory-plugged), observation ports with glass, 6-10 thermocouples (Type K/N in ceramic sheaths) at different heights, pressure taps
Support ring girder at about mid-height on tower steel; shell expansion allowance; metallic expansion joints at ducts
External shell in high-temperature paint; perimeter platforms with toe-boards at each burner and door level; heat shields where walkways pass
hazards_and_safety: Fuel explosion on light-off or after flame failure: BMS per NFPA 85/86 / EN 746-2 / AS 3814 with SIL-rated (IEC 61511) shut-off
Hot shell and radiant heat; CO and NOx near doors
Refractory work: respirable crystalline silica and refractory ceramic fibre dust; heat stress
Hot alumina flushes on furnace trips (inventory drains to HV/coolers)
common_problems: Refractory spalling at cone and burner ports
Flame instability at low load; burner tip erosion
Temperature excursions from feed surges (over-calcination raises alpha and lowers BET)
operating_tips_and_key_points: Control LOI with furnace temperature AND HV residence; check the BET trend daily
Keep the O2 trim narrow: low O2 raises CO and the risk of an ESP trip; high O2 wastes fuel
Follow the refractory dry-out/heat-up curve after relining (typically ~25-50 degC/h, engineering estimate; vendor curve governs)
instrumentation_and_control: TIC furnace outlet -> fuel flow FIC cascade
O2/CO analyser at P04 outlet
Flame scanners per burner; BMS permissives
Shell IR scanner
equipment.drive_and_power: No drive; burners supplied from 15-GS-001; combustion air drawn by ID fan 15-FN
equipment.materials: Carbon steel shell 12-16 mm; high-alumina dense castable/brick working lining; insulating backup
equipment.alternatives: Metso Outotec CFB furnace: fuel injected into a dense circulating bed fluidised by primary air from high-pressure blowers, with a recycle cyclone and seal pot; solids residence ~20-30 min in the loop at ~950-1000 degC.
sources: Raahauge B.E. & Williams F.S. (eds), Smelter Grade Alumina from the Bayer Process, Springer 2022
Hudson L.K. et al., 'Aluminum Oxide', Ullmann's Encyclopedia of Industrial Chemistry (rotary kiln vs stationary calciner energy)
EU JRC BREF Non-Ferrous Metals Industries (2017), alumina chapter

equipment.name: Furnace separation cyclones (P04)
equipment.function: Separate calcined alumina from hot furnace gas at ~950-1050 degC. The gas goes to the P02 riser and the solids to the holding vessel.
equipment.type_selected: Heavily refractory-lined hot cyclones with cast heat-resistant vortex finders
equipment.why_this_type: These are the hottest cyclones in the system. Efficient solids recovery here is vital for product yield and heat economy.
key_dimensions: Gas per cyclone ~105-115 Am3/s at ~1000 degC (engineering estimate)
Inlet ~5.5-6.2 m2 inside lining (e.g. ~2.0 x 3.0 m) for ~18-20 m/s (CORRECTED per review)
Cylinder ID inside lining ~6-7 m, height ~18-24 m (engineering estimate)
Lining ~250-300 mm (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: These work on the same centrifugal principle as the other cyclones, but at full calcination temperature. Gas volume is largest here, so they are the largest cyclones in the tower. The underflow passes through pendulum flaps into the holding vessel. Any carry-over goes with the gas to P02 and returns through the furnace.
details_to_model: Large cyclones high in the tower beside the furnace top; thick refractory, external shell with stiffening rings
Segmented cast vortex finder; roof manway
Dip-legs with refractory-lined pendulum flaps feeding the HV inlet chutes
Air blasters on cone; TCs and pressure taps; expansion joints on inlet and outlet ducts
hazards_and_safety: Highest-temperature solids in the area (~1000 degC): clear blockages only to a written procedure with full thermal PPE
Shell hot spots signal refractory loss: barricade and report
common_problems: Vortex finder segment failure lowers efficiency (higher P02 load, more fines)

equipment.name: Holding vessel (calcination retention vessel)
equipment.function: Holds calcined alumina in a fluidised bed at ~920-1000 degC for extra residence time. Dehydroxylation then finishes at lower temperature, giving lower LOI with high BET and low alpha, and using less fuel.
equipment.type_selected: Vertical refractory-lined bubbling fluidised-bed vessel with nozzle grid and overflow weir/outlet
equipment.why_this_type: A simple fluidised volume gives minutes of residence that the furnace (seconds) cannot. This is how the GSC-HV makes SGA with BET ~70 m2/g at lower temperature.
key_dimensions: ID ~4.5-6 m, bed height ~2-4 m, overall height ~8-12 m (engineering estimate)
Bed inventory ~25-70 t (engineering estimate for 10-30 min at 146 t/h; fluidised density ~0.6-0.8 t/m3)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate (vendor literature cites several to ~30 min)

equipment.working_principle: Alumina from the P04 cyclones falls into a bed kept fluid by air blown up through nozzles in the grid plate. The fluidised bed behaves like a well-mixed liquid. Material flows over a weir or through an adjustable bottom outlet towards cooling cyclone C01, and the bed level (measured by differential pressure) sets the residence time. The remaining hydroxyl groups leave slowly at near-furnace temperature, so LOI drops without the high peak temperature that would turn transition alumina into alpha-alumina and collapse BET. The small flow of HV off-gas joins the furnace gas.
details_to_model: Squat refractory-lined cylinder below the P04 cyclones; 2 inlet chutes on the roof from the P04 flaps
Wind box/plenum below the grid with fluidising air pipe from the blower, isolation and control valve
Grid plate with many cap nozzles (visible in cutaway)
Overflow outlet chute with flow-control gate to the C01 riser; emergency dump outlet
Off-gas vent duct to furnace; DP taps across bed; 3-4 TCs; inspection doors and manways; platform ring
hazards_and_safety: Large inventory of fluid alumina at ~1000 degC: it slumps on a trip, and opening doors may release a flood of hot material
Confined space: entry only when fully cold and drained
common_problems: Nozzle plugging/erosion; bed defluidises on blower failure
instrumentation_and_control: Bed DP level -> outlet gate control
Bed TT
Air flow FIC
equipment.materials: CS shell, dense refractory lining, heat-resistant steel nozzles
sources: FLSmidth GSC with holding vessel vendor literature
Raahauge B.E. & Williams F.S. (eds), Smelter Grade Alumina from the Bayer Process, Springer 2022

equipment.name: Cooling cyclones C01-C04 (suspension coolers)
equipment.function: Cool alumina from ~950-1000 to ~180-280 degC in four counter-current stages while preheating combustion air to ~650-800 degC.
equipment.qty_operating: 4 stages per train; C01 2 cyclones in parallel, C02-C04 1 each (5 cyclones per train, 10 total)
equipment.type_selected: Riser + tangential cyclone stages, refractory-lined (hot) to lightly lined (cold), pendulum flaps
equipment.why_this_type: Direct gas-solid contact recovers most of the product's sensible heat into combustion air. This is the main reason suspension calciners use ~35-40 % less fuel than rotary kilns.
key_dimensions: C01 (x2): ~60-80 Am3/s each at ~650-800 degC; inlet ~3.2-4.2 m2; ID ~5-6 m (engineering estimate)
C02: ~100-110 Am3/s at ~450-550 degC; inlet ~5.3-5.9 m2; ID ~5.8-6.5 m (engineering estimate)
C03: ~75-85 Am3/s at ~280-350 degC; inlet ~4.0-4.5 m2; ID ~5-5.5 m (engineering estimate)
C04: ~60-70 Am3/s at ~160-250 degC; inlet ~3.0-3.8 m2; ID ~4.5-5 m (engineering estimate)
Stage risers ~2.2-3.0 m ID at ~15-20 m/s (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.parameter: Alumina temperature C01 in -> C04 out
operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate; ideal 4-stage balance gives ~160 degC (CORRECTED from 250-320)

operating_parameters.parameter: Air temperature C04 in -> C01 out
operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate; ideal balance ~730 degC at 15 % excess air (CORRECTED from 750-900)

equipment.working_principle: Each stage is a riser plus a cyclone. Hot alumina from the stage above drops into the air rising from the stage below, gives up heat in a second or two, and is separated again in that stage's cyclone. So the alumina moves down C01 -> C04 while the air moves up C04 -> C01, the way a counter-current exchanger works. The air flow carries slightly more heat per degree than the alumina flow, so the air cannot get hotter than about 700-750 degC even with perfect stages. Every leaking flap or shell hot spot lowers that further and raises fuel use. The ID fan draws cold ambient air in at the C04 riser inlet, through an inlet silencer/filter and control damper, together with the warm FBC exhaust air.
details_to_model: Cascade of cyclones on lower tower levels, linked by risers and dip-legs with pendulum flaps
C01/C02 refractory-lined; C03/C04 thinner abrasion lining
Ambient air inlet at the C04 riser: louvred inlet hood with bird screen, silencer and damper; the FBC exhaust air duct joins here
Air blasters on each cone; TCs and pressure taps per stage
Platforms at each cyclone inlet/flap level
hazards_and_safety: Hot alumina and hot air ducts; burn hazards at doors
Noise at the air inlet
common_problems: Flap leakage reduces heat recovery (C01 air temperature falls, fuel use rises)
Erosion at riser elbows (alumina is very abrasive; the alpha fraction is Mohs ~9)

equipment.name: Fluid bed cooler (FBC)
equipment.function: Final cooling of alumina from ~180-280 to ~70-90 degC by indirect water cooling in a fluidised bed, with the heat recovered to hot wash water.
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal rectangular multi-compartment bubbling fluid bed with immersed water-cooled tube bundles
equipment.why_this_type: Fluidised alumina gives high bed-to-tube heat transfer (typically ~200-400 W/m2K, engineering estimate), and the compartments give near counter-current plug flow.
key_dimensions: ~20-35 m long x ~4-6 m wide x ~5-7 m high including plenums (engineering estimate)
4-6 compartments separated by weirs/baffles; ~8-20 removable tube bundles; bed depth ~1.5-2.5 m (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate (CORRECTED from 7-9 for the lower C04 outlet temperature)

equipment.working_principle: Alumina enters at one end and flows through the compartments under weirs or baffles. Air from blowers below the nozzle grid keeps it fluidised. Bundles of tubes carrying cooling water hang in the bed, and the moving particles carry heat to the tube walls very effectively. The water flows counter-current, from the outlet end to the inlet end, to recover the most heat. The bed heats the fluidising air, which leaves through an exhaust duct to the C04 air inlet so its heat is recovered as combustion air. Cooled alumina overflows at the discharge end into the product airslide.
details_to_model: Long rectangular steel box at grade/low level near the tower base, with roof hatches above each tube bundle for crane removal
Tube bundles: U-tube or hairpin bundles hung from roof flanges, each with its own inlet/outlet valves, flow indicator and vent/drain; inlet and outlet headers along the side on a pipe rack
Air plenums (wind boxes) under each compartment with air pipes, manual balancing dampers and pressure gauges; grid with cap nozzles
Inlet chute from C04 at one end; overflow outlet box at the other end with discharge gate to the airslide; bottom drain gates per compartment
Exhaust air outlet nozzle on the roof to the duct; inspection doors and sight glasses; bed TCs and DP taps per compartment
Gantry/monorail crane above the roof for bundle pulling; walkway platform along the roof
hazards_and_safety: Hot fluidised alumina flows like water: lock out and drain before entry
Tube leak: steam/water in the hot bed causes lumps, pressure surges and wet product
Pinch/crush hazards during bundle lifting
common_problems: Tube erosion near nozzles; tube leaks
Nozzle blockage; defluidisation and channelling
operating_tips_and_key_points: Watch bed humidity, exhaust dew point and loop make-up: a rising trend is the early warning of a tube leak. Isolate that bundle and run on the others
instrumentation_and_control: Product outlet TT (alarm >100 degC)
Per-bundle FI, closed-loop conductivity/make-up monitor
Compartment DP
equipment.materials: CS casing; CS or low-alloy tubes with wear shields; stainless nozzles
sources: FLSmidth / Metso Outotec FBC vendor literature
Kunii D. & Levenspiel O., Fluidization Engineering, 2nd ed. (bed-to-tube heat transfer)

equipment.name: FBC and holding-vessel fluidising air blowers
equipment.function: Supply fluidising air to the FBC compartments and the holding vessel.
equipment.type_selected: Multistage centrifugal or rotary-lobe (Roots) blowers with inlet filter/silencer; HV branch on a higher-pressure blower or booster
equipment.why_this_type: They deliver the moderate pressure (20-50 kPa) at steady flow that fluidisation needs. A standby is essential because a collapsed bed stops the train.
key_dimensions: Packaged skid ~4 x 2 x 2.5 m each with acoustic enclosure (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: A rotary-lobe blower traps pockets of air and pushes them out (positive displacement). A multistage centrifugal raises pressure across several impellers in series. Either way, filtered ambient air is compressed and sent through a header to the plenums of each fluid-bed compartment and the HV. Each branch has flow control and a non-return valve. The standby starts automatically on low header pressure.
details_to_model: Blower on baseplate with motor, V-belt or direct coupling, guard
Inlet filter-silencer, discharge silencer, relief valve, non-return valve, isolation butterfly
Acoustic enclosure with ventilation fan; pressure and temperature gauges
hazards_and_safety: Noise >85 dB(A) outside enclosures
Rotating parts; hot discharge pipe (~80-120 degC)

equipment.name: Electrostatic precipitator (calciner off-gas)
equipment.function: Remove alumina/hydrate dust from the calciner off-gas to meet emission limits and recover product.
equipment.type_selected: Dry horizontal-flow plate-type ESP, 1 casing with 2 parallel chambers, 4 fields in series, rigid discharge electrodes, tumbling-hammer rapping
equipment.why_this_type: An ESP handles the large, humid, warm gas volume at low pressure drop (~0.2-0.4 kPa), and calciner dust in humid gas has a resistivity that suits ESP collection. Fabric filters are an alternative but struggle with the gas moisture and dew point (~80 degC).
key_dimensions: Gas flow area ~140-170 m2 for ~0.8-1.0 m/s, e.g. ~30-34 gas passages at 400 mm spacing x ~12.5-13.5 m plate height (CORRECTED per review)
Casing ~14-17 m wide x ~16-19 m high above hoppers x ~25-32 m long incl. inlet/outlet transitions; hoppers ~6-8 m deep (engineering estimate)
4 fields of ~4-5 m length; collecting area ~11,000-15,000 m2 (SCA ~80-110 s/m at ~135 Am3/s) (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: typical licence limits; EU BREF NFM 2017 BAT-AEL is lower (verify clause)

equipment.working_principle: High negative DC voltage on the discharge electrodes creates a corona that charges the dust as the gas passes slowly (about 0.8-1.0 m/s) between earthed collecting plates. The charged particles migrate to the plates and build up a layer, which periodic hammer rapping knocks into the hoppers below. Each field removes most of the dust that is left, so four fields in series collect more than 99.9 %. Perforated distribution screens at the inlet spread the flow evenly over the whole section. CO in the gas is a key hazard, because a spark in a combustible mixture can cause an explosion. The T/R sets therefore trip automatically on high CO.
details_to_model: Large rectangular box casing on columns, split internally into 2 chambers; inlet transition (funnel) with 2-3 perforated distribution screens; outlet transition

Roof: one transformer-rectifier set per field per chamber (oil-filled tank with HV bushing in bus duct), insulator housings with heaters and purge-air fans, rapping drive motors for discharge electrodes
Side: rapping gear motors driving tumbling-hammer shafts for the collecting plates
Pyramidal hoppers (e.g., 2 across x 4 along), each with level probe, heater pads, poke hole and outlet to rotary valve/screw conveyor
Access doors on each field with Castell key interlock and earthing switch; stairs to the roof penthouse; full insulation and cladding (~100 mm mineral wool + profiled sheeting)
Cutaway internals: collecting plates (C-profile strips), discharge electrode frames with pipe-and-spike electrodes, gas flow baffles
hazards_and_safety: High voltage (~70-100 kV DC): access only through the key-interlock sequence (T/R off, earth switch closed, key released), plus earthing sticks
CO explosion risk: CO analyser at inlet; T/R trip on high CO (typical alarm ~0.3-0.5 %, trip ~0.5-1.0 % vol, site-specific engineering estimate)
Hot dust in hoppers (flows freely, burns); confined space; heavy rapping hammers
common_problems: Hopper bridging from condensation when cold
Broken discharge electrode short-circuiting a field
Emission spikes after rapping (rapping puffs)
instrumentation_and_control: Per-field kV/mA, spark rate; automatic voltage control
Inlet CO/O2; outlet opacity/dust monitor (in stack)
Hopper level high alarms
equipment.materials: CS casing, CS plates/electrodes, porcelain/alumina-ceramic insulators
sources: EU JRC BREF Non-Ferrous Metals Industries (2017)
White H.J., Industrial Electrostatic Precipitation; Parker K.R., Applied Electrostatic Precipitation

equipment.name: ESP dust collection and return system
equipment.function: Collect ESP hopper dust and return it to the calciner (P02 riser) for processing.
equipment.qty_operating: Per train: ~8 hopper rotary valves, ~2 collecting screws, 1 dust bin + 1 dense-phase blow tank
equipment.qty_standby: Return conveyor: 1 shared standby or bypass to the off-spec silo (engineering estimate)
equipment.type_selected: Hopper rotary valves -> collecting screw conveyors -> dust bin -> dense-phase blow tank to P02 riser
equipment.why_this_type: ESP dust is mostly uncalcined fine hydrate (high LOI), so it must be recalcined, not sent to product. Pneumatic return reaches the high injection point in the tower.
key_dimensions: Collecting screws ~400-500 mm dia; dust bin ~30-60 m3; blow tank ~2-4 m3 (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Rotary airlock valves let dust out of the hoppers without letting air into the ESP, which is under suction. Screw conveyors gather the dust into a small bin. A blow tank below it fills, closes and is pressurised, then pushes the dust in batches through a pipeline to the injection point on the P02 riser.
details_to_model: Rotary valves under each hopper with gear motors; inclined collecting screws under the hopper rows
Dust bin with vent filter; blow tank with dome inlet valve, vent valve, aeration pad, outlet valve, air control panel
DN 100-150 conveying line routed up the tower with long-radius wear-resistant bends
hazards_and_safety: Hot fine dust inhalation; pressurised vessel (do not open under pressure)
sources: Mills D., Pneumatic Conveying Design Guide, 2nd ed.

equipment.name: Calciner induced-draft (ID) fan
equipment.function: Draws all gas through the coolers, furnace, preheaters, dryer and ESP and discharges it to the stack. It sets the system draft and throughput.
equipment.type_selected: Large single- (or double-) inlet centrifugal fan, backward-curved/aerofoil impeller, MV motor with VFD
equipment.why_this_type: It moves a high volume at ~9-13 kPa with variable-speed control. Placed after the ESP, it handles clean gas, so wear is low.
key_dimensions: Impeller diameter ~3.2-4.5 m; casing height ~7-9 m (engineering estimate)
Motor ~2.2-2.8 MW, 6.6-11 kV (engineering estimate: 140 Am3/s x 11 kPa / 0.82 = ~1.9 MW shaft) (CORRECTED from 1.5-2.5 MW)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate: 7 cyclone stages at ~1.0-1.8 kPa + venturi ~1.5-2.5 + furnace/HV + ESP + ducts (CORRECTED from 8-11)

equipment.working_principle: The rotating impeller flings gas outward, raising its pressure in the spiral (volute) casing and creating suction throughout the calciner. Fan speed sets total gas flow, which together with fuel rate sets furnace O2 and calciner capacity. Every stage is under suction, so leaks draw air in rather than letting hot dust out. Leaks still cost fuel and fan capacity.
details_to_model: Spiral volute casing on a concrete plinth; inlet box with multi-louvre isolation damper and flexible joint; outlet evase to the stack duct
Overhung or centre-hung impeller on two pedestal bearings (oil-lubricated, with lube oil unit), each with RTDs and vibration probes
Large MV motor with coupling and guard; VFD in e-house
Casing insulated and clad; drain; inspection door; maintenance monorail/crane over the fan
hazards_and_safety: Rotating machinery; overspeed/imbalance; noise >85 dB(A)
Hot casing; positive pressure on the stack side
common_problems: Imbalance from dust build-up when ESP efficiency falls; bearing temperature rise
instrumentation_and_control: Vibration (proximity probes/accelerometers) and bearing TT with trips
Speed control from the furnace draft/O2 controller

equipment.name: Calciner stack with CEMS
equipment.function: Disperses the cleaned off-gas and carries the continuous emission monitoring system (CEMS).
equipment.qty_operating: 2 (1 per train), or 1 concrete windshield with 2 steel flues
equipment.type_selected: Self-supporting insulated steel stack with sampling platforms
equipment.why_this_type: Simple. Insulation keeps the flue above the dew point and so avoids condensation and corrosion.
key_dimensions: Flue ID ~3.0-3.5 m (exit velocity ~13-18 m/s at ~125 Am3/s) (engineering estimate)
Height ~60-90 m, set by dispersion modelling/regulation (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Buoyant, fast-moving gas leaves well above ground, so pollutants are diluted before they reach ground level. The CEMS continuously measures dust, O2, CO, NOx (and SO2 if oil-fired), flow, temperature and moisture for compliance reporting.
details_to_model: Tapered base with breech inlet from the ID fan duct; access door; condensate drain
Sampling platform at the required straight-run position with 4 sampling ports (ISO 9096 / AS 4323.1 / US EPA Method 1)
CEMS shelter at base; analyser probes; caged ladder or ladder with fall-arrest rail; rest platforms
Aircraft warning lights, lightning rod/earthing, insulated and clad shell
hazards_and_safety: Work at height; flue gas exposure at sampling ports (CO, low O2, heat)

equipment.name: Fuel gas pressure-reducing, metering and safety shut-off skid (with BMS)
equipment.function: Conditions, meters and safely isolates the natural gas supply to the calciner burners.
equipment.type_selected: Outdoor skid: ESD valve, filter-separator, heater (if needed), PRV streams with slam-shut, metering, per-train safety shut-off valve trains
equipment.why_this_type: The codes (NFPA 85/86, EN 746-2, AS 3814) require proven-closure double block and vent valves, purge permissives and flame supervision.
key_dimensions: Skid ~15-20 m x 6-8 m in a fenced area, set back from ignition sources per hazardous-area classification (engineering estimate)
Main pipe DN 250-300 (engineering estimate for ~25,000 Nm3/h)
equipment.working_principle: Gas passes an emergency shutdown valve and a filter, then pressure-reducing runs, each with a monitor regulator and a slam-shut valve against overpressure. It is metered (ultrasonic or turbine meter) and sent to each train. At each burner header the burner management system (BMS) controls two automatic shut-off valves with a vent valve between them (double block and bleed). They open only after a proven purge and ignition sequence. They close in under 1 s on flame failure, low air flow or ESD.
details_to_model: Yellow-painted gas pipework on low supports; filter-separator vessel; regulator runs with slam-shuts and relief valves venting via a vent stack
Flow meter run with straight lengths; pressure/temperature gauges and transmitters
Per-train valve trains on the furnace burner platform: manual isolation, SSOV pair, vent valve, pressure switches, control valve
Gas detectors, hazardous-area signage, fence, emergency stop
hazards_and_safety: Gas explosion/fire; hazardous area Zone 2 per IEC 60079-10-1
Pressure; venting near personnel
instrumentation_and_control: BMS PLC (SIL-rated per IEC 61511), valve proving system, gas detection

equipment.name: FBC cooling-water circuit: circulation pumps, plate heat exchangers, cooling tower
equipment.function: Circulate closed-loop water through the FBC bundles, pass the heat to process wash water in plate exchangers, and reject any surplus in a cooling tower.
equipment.qty_operating: Pumps 1 per train; HX 1 per train; cooling tower 1 common multi-cell (2-3 cells)
equipment.qty_standby: Pumps 1 per train; cooling tower 1 cell spare (engineering estimate)
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal end-suction centrifugal pumps (ISO 5199/ISO 2858); gasketed plate heat exchangers; induced-draft counterflow cooling tower
equipment.why_this_type: Standard clean-water service. Plate exchangers give a close temperature approach for heat recovery to the hydrate wash water.
key_dimensions: Pumps ~200-300 m3/h at ~35-50 m, 37-75 kW (engineering estimate)
Plate HX frames ~3 x 1 x 3 m (engineering estimate)
Cooling tower cells ~8-10 m x 8-10 m in plan, fans ~5-7 m dia (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate (CORRECTED from 250-400 to match 5-8 MW at dT 20-30 K)

equipment.working_principle: Centrifugal pumps drive treated water through the FBC tube bundles, where it heats to about 55-70 degC. In the plate heat exchangers it heats the hydrate filter wash water across thin corrugated plates in counter-current. Any remaining heat is rejected in the cooling tower. An expansion tank with a nitrogen or air cushion, a side-stream filter and corrosion-inhibitor dosing protect the loop.
details_to_model: Pump sets on concrete plinths with suction strainers, isolation valves, check valves, pressure gauges, coupling guards
Plate HX frames with tie-bolts and nozzles on the fixed plate
Cooling tower with fan stacks, motors/gearboxes, louvres, basin, make-up and blowdown; expansion tank and dosing skid
hazards_and_safety: Rotating equipment; hot water (scald risk) at ~70 degC; Legionella control in the cooling tower

equipment.name: Calciner plant and instrument air compressors (incl. air-blaster supply)
equipment.function: Provide dry compressed air for instruments, air blasters, purge air and pneumatic actuators.
equipment.type_selected: Oil-free rotary screw compressors with refrigerant/desiccant dryers and receivers
equipment.why_this_type: Oil-free air avoids contaminating the alumina, and the air blasters need a reliable 6-8 bar supply.
key_dimensions: Each ~2,000-4,000 Nm3/h, 250-450 kW; receivers ~10-20 m3 (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Two meshing screw rotors compress the air with no oil in the compression chamber. The air is cooled, dried, stored in receivers and piped to the tower. Each air blaster there has its own small receiver. When its solenoid valve fires, the blaster dumps that receiver through a nozzle into the cyclone cone to knock off build-ups.
details_to_model: Compressor packages in a compressor house; dryers; vertical receivers with safety valves
Air blaster tanks (~50-150 L) on cyclone cones with quick-dump valves and nozzle pipes (~20-40 per train)
hazards_and_safety: Air blaster discharge can injure and blow out hot dust: isolate and depressurise before cone or door work
sources: Martin Engineering / Global Manufacturing air cannon practice

equipment.name: Calciner product auto-sampler
equipment.function: Takes representative samples of each train's product for process control (LOI, BET, alpha, PSD, Na2O).
equipment.type_selected: Timed cross-stream/screw-type sampler in FBC discharge airslide, with pneumatic sample delivery to laboratory
equipment.why_this_type: Each train's product must be monitored separately to adjust that train's furnace temperature and HV.
key_dimensions: Compact enclosure ~1 x 1 x 1.5 m on airslide (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: A cutter or screw probe periodically takes a slice of the flowing alumina. The increments are combined into a composite, which a pneumatic tube sends to the laboratory. Results feed back to the furnace temperature set point.
details_to_model: Sampler body on the airslide with motor/actuator, sample bottle carousel or pneumatic tube send station
hazards_and_safety: Hot alumina (up to ~90 degC); moving cutter
sources: ISO 2927 (alumina sampling), ISO 806 (LOI), ISO 8008 (BET), ISO 2926 (sieve analysis) - verify current editions

equipment.name: Calciner area sump pumps
equipment.function: Return wash-down water and spilled hydrate/alumina slurry from area bunds to process.
equipment.type_selected: Vertical cantilever slurry sump pumps (no submerged bearings), rubber/hard-metal wetted parts
equipment.why_this_type: Robust for intermittent abrasive slurry, with no submerged bearings or seals.
key_dimensions: ~30-80 m3/h at ~20-30 m; 15-30 kW; sump ~3 x 3 x 3 m (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: The motor sits on a mounting plate above the sump and drives a long cantilevered shaft down to an impeller near the bottom, which pumps the slurry back to process. Sump level starts and stops the pump.
details_to_model: Grated sump pit with pump mounting plate, motor on top, discharge pipe with check and isolation valves, level float/radar
hazards_and_safety: Open pit when grating is removed; mildly caustic slurry
sources: Weir Warman / Metso slurry pump practice

equipment.name: Calciner tower structure, stair tower, goods/passenger lift and maintenance hoists
equipment.function: Supports cyclones, furnace, HV and ducts, and provides access and maintenance lifting.
equipment.type_selected: Braced structural-steel tower (or concrete core + steel) with grated floors, external stair tower and rack-and-pinion/traction lift
equipment.why_this_type: It gives access to ~10-14 working levels, and the lift moves refractory, flaps and vortex-finder segments.
key_dimensions: Footprint ~25-30 m x 25-35 m; height to top of P01/P02 cyclones ~60-80 m (engineering estimate)
Lift capacity ~1.5-2.5 t (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.value: wind/cyclonic and seismic per AS 1170 / IS 875 / IS 1893

equipment.working_principle: The steel frame carries the hot vessels on support rings and lugs and lets them grow thermally. Monorails and davits over each cyclone roof lower internals through the hatches and onto the lift.
details_to_model: Column/beam grid with diagonal bracing; grating floors, handrails with kick-plates; stair tower with landings at every floor
Lift shaft with cage; monorail beams with chain hoists above cyclone roofs and the FBC; partial wall cladding; emergency lighting; safety showers at each level near caustic/hot work
hazards_and_safety: Work at height; dropped objects; heat stress on upper levels; escape routes (2 per level)
sources: AS 1170 / IS 875 / IS 1893; AS 1657 (platforms, stairs, ladders)

areas.layout_notes: Two calciner towers side by side, ~40-60 m centre-to-centre (engineering estimate), each with its ESP, ID fan and stack in line downstream. The gas path runs away from the control room, towards the prevailing downwind side. Tower footprint ~25-30 x 25-35 m, height ~60-80 m. Cyclone order from the top: P01 (dryer cyclones) and P02 on the top levels, P04 cyclones and furnace top in the middle-upper levels, HV mid-level, C01-C04 descending, FBC at grade. The A14 product filters sit on an adjacent structure or on top of the calciner feed building, so cake discharges directly into the feed bins. The two hydrate slurry storage tanks (15-TK-001/002, ~22-24 m dia) stand in a bund beside the A14 filter building, ~50-100 m from the towers, with the reclaim pump bay between them. ESP ~20-40 m from the tower, ID fan at grade beside the ESP outlet, stack ~10-20 m beyond. Fuel gas skid in a fenced area >=15-30 m from ignition sources (hazardous-area study). Cooling tower and pumps at grade near the FBC. Main pipe rack (NG, cooling water, compressed air, power and control cables) along the calciner row, ~6-8 m high, linking to A14 and A16. Product airslides discharge to dense-phase vessels at the tower base, with pipelines ~200-500 m to the product silos (A16). Common calciner control room/e-house ~50-100 m from the towers, outside the hazardous area and the hot-alumina spill zone. Heavy-vehicle roads around each tower for cranes (refractory relines), with laydown area.
interfaces: A13 Precipitation/classification: product hydrate slurry diverted to the 15-TK outage buffer; hydrate strength and PSD govern product fines (-45 um) and attrition index

A14 Hydrate filtration/washing: wet hydrate feed (moisture and soda set calciner fuel use and product Na2O); the filters must have ~110-120 % capacity to work down the hydrate buffer; hot wash water from FBC heat recovery
A16 Product storage & conveying: calcined alumina from FBC airslides; off-spec diversion; off-spec return to P02

Utilities (A20): natural gas supply (fuel oil from the A17 port tank farm as backup), MV power (~10-14 MW connected for 2 trains, engineering estimate), cooling water make-up, demineralised water, compressed air
Laboratory: LOI, MOI, BET, alpha, PSD, chemistry (ISO methods)
Environmental: stack CEMS reporting; ESP dust return

areas.purpose: Move hot SGA gently from the calciner fluid bed coolers to the refinery product silos and store ~7 days of production. Keep off-spec material separate, including returns from the port. Reclaim product to the covered overland conveyor to the port, with an optional road-tanker loadout. Main design constraints: low particle attrition (to protect the -45 um specification), no moisture pick-up or contamination (Fe, Si, organics), and enclosed, dust-free handling.
areas.process_description: 1) Each FBC discharges into an enclosed airslide feeding a twin-vessel dense-phase pneumatic conveying system, one line per calciner. 2) Dense-phase conveying moves alumina at low velocity (~3-10 m/s, engineering estimate) with high solids loading, which limits particle breakage. Lean-phase airlifts are avoided where possible because they make fines. 3) The pipelines discharge at the silo roofs into 2 x 20,000 t concrete product silos (40,000 t, ~7 days). A diverter can send start-up or off-spec alumina (e.g., high LOI after a trip) to a 3,000-5,000 t off-spec silo. That silo also takes rejects trucked back from the port, and its contents are reprocessed in controlled amounts through the calciner (P02 return) or into digestion. 4) Silo vent air (conveying air) passes through pulse-jet bag filters, and the dust returns to the silo. 5) Silo bottoms have aerated sectors (sequential aeration) with flow-control gates discharging into airslides and onto an enclosed 1,200 mm reclaim belt conveyor. The conveyor carries a belt scale, a self-cleaning magnet (protects the Fe spec) and a sampler. 6) The reclaim conveyor feeds the covered 1,200 mm overland conveyor to the port (A17), ~8 km (coastal-refinery basis, as at Alunorte-Vila do Conde, Gove and QAL). It is designed for ~800 t/h and runs ~8-10 h/d. 7) An optional road tanker loadout serves domestic smelters. SGA properties that matter: loose bulk density ~0.95-1.05 t/m3, angle of repose ~30-35 deg, low surcharge angle on belts (~5-10 deg), very abrasive, fluidisable (Geldart A/B) and hygroscopic (MOI rises in humid air). All handling is therefore enclosed. Belts are sized for ~55-65 % of the CEMA/ISO 5048 cross-section at a 10 deg surcharge.
