equipment.name: FBC discharge airslides and airslide blowers
equipment.function: Convey cooled alumina by gravity and fluidisation from the FBC outlets to the dense-phase vessel feed hoppers.
equipment.type_selected: Enclosed air-gravity conveyor (airslide) with woven polyester or ceramic porous membrane
equipment.why_this_type: Low power, almost no attrition and fully enclosed. Ideal for fluidisable alumina on a downward slope.
key_dimensions: Width ~400-600 mm; slope ~4-8 deg; lengths ~10-40 m (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.value: ~2-3 Nm3/min per m2 of fabric at ~3-6 kPa

equipment.working_principle: A porous fabric splits a rectangular trough horizontally into two chambers. Low-pressure air blown into the lower chamber passes up through the fabric and fluidises the alumina above it. The fluidised alumina then flows like a liquid down the gentle slope. The upper chamber vents to a dust filter.
details_to_model: Two-piece flanged rectangular steel trough with bolted flanges every ~2-3 m and the fabric clamped between
Air inlet stubs with butterfly valves under the trough; vent nozzles on top
Flow control gates, inspection windows/sight glasses; supports set to the slope; small centrifugal fan/blower with filter
hazards_and_safety: Hot alumina at ~80 degC flows freely if a cover is opened; dust

equipment.name: Dense-phase pneumatic conveying vessels (twin blow tanks per line) with line diverters
equipment.function: Transport SGA from each calciner to the product or off-spec silos with low attrition.
equipment.qty_standby: Cross-connection lets one line deliver to either silo; no idle spare line (engineering estimate)
equipment.type_selected: Twin pressure-vessel (blow tank) dense-phase system, alternating fill/convey for quasi-continuous flow
equipment.why_this_type: Low conveying velocity reduces particle breakage and pipe wear compared with lean-phase conveying or airlifts. The pipe can be routed flexibly up ~50-60 m to the silo roofs.
key_dimensions: Each vessel ~8-15 m3, ~2.5-3 m dia, ~4-5 m tall with conical bottom (engineering estimate)
Design pressure ~6 bar(g); ASME VIII Div 1 / AS 1210
Conveying distance ~200-500 m, lift ~50-60 m (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: While one vessel conveys, the other fills by gravity from the feed hopper through its inlet valve, with its vent valve open. When it is full (load cells or level probe), the inlet and vent close and the vessel is pressurised with air. The outlet valve then opens and pushes a dense, plug-like stream of alumina through the pipeline. When the vessel pressure drops (vessel empty), the outlet closes and the vessel vents. The two vessels alternate, so delivery to the silo is nearly continuous. Pipeline diverters at the silo roof select the product or off-spec silo.
details_to_model: Vertical pressure vessels in a steel frame below the airslide feed hopper; top dome/ball inlet valve with pneumatic actuator
Vent valve and vent line back to the hopper; aeration cone/pad at the bottom; outlet valve to the pipeline; pressure-vessel nameplate, safety valve
Load cells or level probes; air control panel (pressure regulators, flow orifices, solenoids) in a cabinet

Pipeline DN 250-350 (stepped), ceramic-lined or hardened long-radius bends, pipe supports with sliding shoes, routed on the rack and up the silo stair tower; booster-air injection points along the line
Two-way pipeline diverter valves (16-DV) on the silo-roof bridge with position switches
hazards_and_safety: Pressure vessel: never open hatches under pressure; PSV testing
Clearing a pipeline blockage under pressure is dangerous: depressurise first
Noise from venting
common_problems: Line blockage after a feed surge or loss of air
Bend wear
instrumentation_and_control: PLC sequence; pressure transmitters on vessel and line; line-blockage detection (high pressure/time)
equipment.materials: CS vessel; ceramic/alloy wear bends; abrasion-resistant valve seats
equipment.alternatives: Bucket elevator + enclosed belt conveyor + airslides (lower power, more maintenance); airlift (lean phase, more attrition).
sources: Mills D., Pneumatic Conveying Design Guide, 2nd ed.
Klinzing G.E. et al., Pneumatic Conveying of Solids

equipment.name: Conveying air compressors with dryers and receivers
equipment.function: Supply dry, oil-free air for dense-phase conveying and silo aeration boost.
equipment.type_selected: Oil-free rotary screw compressors (VFD on one), refrigerated dryers, vertical receivers
equipment.why_this_type: Oil-free, dry air keeps the alumina clean and stops moisture pick-up (MOI).
key_dimensions: Each ~60-90 Nm3/min, ~350-500 kW; receivers ~20-30 m3 (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Screw compressors supply a ring main and receivers. Each conveying line draws its air through pressure regulators. The receivers cover the sudden demand when a blow tank pressurises.
details_to_model: Compressor house with packages, aftercoolers, dryers, receivers with PSVs and drains, ring-main headers
hazards_and_safety: Noise; stored pressure energy; hot surfaces

equipment.name: Refinery product alumina silos
equipment.function: Store SGA (2 x ~20,000 t) as a buffer between calcination and despatch to the port.
equipment.type_selected: Slip-formed reinforced-concrete silos with central inverted cone and aerated annular floor (multi-sector sequential aeration)
equipment.why_this_type: Concrete silos store a large volume on a small footprint. An aerated floor with a central cone gives near-complete discharge of fluidisable alumina and first-in-first-out flow.
key_dimensions: ID ~26-28 m; wall height ~40-50 m; overall height including roof house ~50-60 m (engineering estimate: 20,000 t / ~1.0 t/m3 = ~20,000 m3 + cone and freeboard)
8-12 aeration sectors (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Alumina enters at the roof. To discharge, air is blown in turn into floor sectors through porous aeration panels or airslides that slope towards outlets in a central inverted cone. The alumina above the active sectors fluidises and flows to the outlets. Flow-control gates meter it into the discharge airslides. Rotating the active sector draws the silo down evenly and avoids dead zones. The roof vent filter handles the displaced air plus the conveying air.
details_to_model: Tall concrete cylinder with smooth slipform finish; flat or conical steel/concrete roof with roof house (filters, inlet piping, diverters)
External stair tower with landings (or internal stairs in an annex) plus personnel/goods lift; roof handrails
Radar level gauges, pressure/vacuum relief valve, roof manholes, lightning protection
Base: discharge tunnel or ring with outlet gates (manual slide gate + pneumatic flow-control gate), aeration piping manifold with a solenoid valve per sector, inspection doors into the cone
Silo-top pulse-jet bag filter with fan and discharge rotary valve back to the silo
hazards_and_safety: Silo entry: engulfment and risk of drowning in fluidised alumina. Never enter while aeration is possible (isolate blowers); confined-space permit
Work at height on the roof; structural overpressure if the vent filter blinds
common_problems: Dead zones/caking from moisture ingress; sector valve failure
Segregation of fines near walls and at the filter return
operating_tips_and_key_points: Rotate the silos (fill/reclaim) to keep stock fresh; keep roof hatches closed in rain (hygroscopic product)
instrumentation_and_control: Radar LT; vent filter DP; sector aeration sequencer; flow-gate position
equipment.materials: Reinforced concrete; steel roof; polyester/ceramic aeration panels
sources: Claudius Peters / IBAU silo technology literature

equipment.name: Silo aeration blowers
equipment.function: Supply low-pressure aeration air to the product and off-spec silo floors and discharge airslides.
equipment.type_selected: Rotary-lobe (Roots) blowers with inlet filter/silencer, aftercooler optional, in an acoustic enclosure
equipment.why_this_type: Positive-displacement blowers give a steady flow at 0.5-0.8 bar(g) whatever the bed resistance.
key_dimensions: ~3,000-6,000 Nm3/h each, 75-160 kW (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: The blowers feed a header to the silo-base aeration manifolds. A sequencer opens each sector valve in turn, so only part of the silo floor is aerated at any time. Dry air matters, because moist air raises product MOI.
details_to_model: Blower house at silo base: blowers on baseplates with V-belt drive and guard, filter-silencers, relief and non-return valves, header with isolation valves
hazards_and_safety: Noise; rotating parts; hot discharge pipe

equipment.name: Off-spec alumina silo
equipment.function: Receive start-up/upset or contaminated alumina, including port rejects, for controlled reprocessing.
equipment.type_selected: Steel silo with aerated cone bottom, rotary feeder and truck blow-off receiving connection
equipment.why_this_type: Keeps off-spec material out of the product silos while still recovering it.
key_dimensions: ~3,000-5,000 t; ~14-16 m dia x ~25-30 m (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: A diverter on the dense-phase line sends off-spec alumina here. Pressure-discharge road tankers can also blow port rejects in through a fill pipe. The material is later fed slowly back into the calciner (via the ESP dust-return system to the P02 riser) or to digestion, so that product quality is not disturbed.
details_to_model: Steel shell on a skirt or columns, conical aerated bottom, rotary feeder and small dense-phase return vessel; vent filter; ladder/stairs
Truck bay with DN 100 blow-off fill pipe, quick coupling, vent filter interlock and spill tray
hazards_and_safety: As for the product silos; tanker hose whip during blow-off

equipment.name: Silo vent and transfer-point dust collectors
equipment.function: Clean the displaced/conveying air from silos and transfer points and return the dust to process.
equipment.type_selected: Pulse-jet bag filters (polyester or PTFE-membrane bags) with exhaust fans
equipment.why_this_type: High efficiency (<10-20 mg/Nm3) on fine alumina dust, plus product recovery.
key_dimensions: Silo vent filters ~300-600 m2 cloth each; transfer collectors ~100-300 m2 (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate; typical BAT for fabric filters

equipment.working_principle: Dusty air passes through the filter bags from outside to inside, and the dust collects on the bag surface. Short pulses of compressed air fired into the bags in sequence knock the dust off into the hopper, and a rotary valve returns it to process.
details_to_model: Rectangular housing with hopper, clean-air plenum with walk-in or top-access doors, pulse valves and header tank, rotary valve, fan with stack, DP gauge
hazards_and_safety: Confined space; compressed air; falls from roof access

equipment.name: Silo reclaim conveyor with belt scale, tramp-iron magnet and sampler
equipment.function: Collect alumina from the silo discharges and deliver it to the overland conveyor at a measured rate.
equipment.type_selected: Enclosed troughed belt conveyor (1,200 mm), covered gallery, belt scale, self-cleaning overband magnet, cross-belt sampler
equipment.why_this_type: Gentle transport at a high rate. The magnet protects the Fe2O3 product spec and the scale gives inventory control.
key_dimensions: Belt 1,200 mm, ~3.0-3.5 m/s, length ~150-400 m (CORRECTED from 1,050 mm, engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate: 800/(0.95 x 3,600 x 3.15) = 0.074 m2 required vs ~0.13 m2 CEMA area for 1,200 mm, 35 deg trough, 10 deg surcharge = ~57 % fill
engineering estimate: fluidisable alumina runs back on steep belts

equipment.working_principle: A rubber belt on troughed idlers carries alumina from the silo outlets to the transfer tower. The belt scale (load cells under weigh idlers plus a speed sensor) totals the tonnage. An overband magnet lifts out any tramp iron. A cross-belt sampler periodically sweeps a full cross-section of the stream.
details_to_model: Conveyor stringers, 3-roll troughing idlers at ~1.2 m pitch, return idlers ~3 m, hood covers/enclosed gallery with walkway
Head pulley drive (motor, fluid coupling/VFD, gearbox), tail pulley, gravity take-up, primary/secondary belt cleaners, skirt boards
Pull-wire emergency stops along both sides, belt drift and speed switches, guards on all pulleys
Belt scale weigh frame; magnet with cross-belt and reject chute; sampler hammer-cutter
hazards_and_safety: Conveyor nip points (guarding per AS 4024 / ISO 14120); pull-wire stops; lockout
Dust
sources: CEMA Belt Conveyors for Bulk Materials, 7th ed.

equipment.name: Overland covered belt conveyor to port (with transfer towers)
equipment.function: Transport SGA from the refinery silos to the port silos.
equipment.qty_standby: 0 (silo buffers at both ends cover outages)
equipment.type_selected: Covered troughed steel-cord belt conveyor (1,200 mm) on ground-level and elevated trestles, hooded with walkway (pipe conveyor alternative)
equipment.why_this_type: The lowest-cost enclosed, low-attrition bulk transport for ~2 Mt/yr over a few km. Rail with covered hopper or pressure-discharge wagons is the alternative for inland refineries (e.g., Worsley-Bunbury ~55 km; Damanjodi-Visakhapatnam).
key_dimensions: Length ~8 km assumed (coastal-refinery basis; site-specific, engineering estimate)
Belt 1,200 mm ST1250-ST2000 steel cord, ~3.5-4 m/s (CORRECTED from 1,050 mm; ~50-60 % fill) (engineering estimate)
Installed drive power ~1.0-1.4 MW, e.g. 2-3 x 450 kW per flight set (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate: 5,480 t/d / 800 t/h = ~7 h + margin

equipment.working_principle: This is the same principle as the reclaim conveyor, over a long distance. Low-friction idlers and a steel-cord belt carry the high belt tension. VFD drives give a controlled soft start, and a gravity take-up holds belt tension. Steel hoods keep rain off the hygroscopic product and stop wind blowing dust.
details_to_model: Continuous arched steel hoods on the carry side, one-side walkway with handrail, crossover stairs every ~300-500 m
Elevated trusses at road/rail crossings; transfer towers with chutes, dust collectors, enclosed walls
Drive station with 2-3 motors, gearboxes, brakes, holdback; gravity take-up tower with counterweight
Pull-wire switches every ~50 m both sides, drift switches, rip detection, fire detection (linear heat), lighting
Pipe track alongside carrying the caustic and fuel-oil pipelines and power/fibre
hazards_and_safety: Entrapment at idlers/pulleys; long isolation distances (radio + local isolators)
Heavy vehicles at crossings
sources: CEMA Belt Conveyors for Bulk Materials, 7th ed.

equipment.name: Road tanker alumina loadout (optional, domestic market)
equipment.function: Load SGA into pressure-discharge bulk tankers for local smelters.
equipment.type_selected: Telescopic loading spout with integrated dust extraction over a weighbridge
equipment.why_this_type: Dust-free loading of enclosed bulk tankers.
key_dimensions: Loading rate ~150-300 t/h; weighbridge 18-25 m (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: The spout lowers onto the tanker hatch and alumina flows from an airslide through the inner cone. Displaced air is drawn back through the outer annulus to a filter. Level sensing stops the flow when the tanker is full.
details_to_model: Small feed bin, flow gate, telescopic bellows spout with winch, hatch-seal cone, extraction fan/filter, weighbridge, traffic lights, fall-protection gantry
hazards_and_safety: Work at height on tanker roofs (fall-arrest gantry); vehicle movements

areas.layout_notes: Product silos ~150-400 m from the calciner towers, at the refinery boundary on the port side to shorten the overland route and the dense-phase lines. The silos stand in a row ~10-15 m apart, sharing a stair/lift tower, with a roof-level bridge carrying the pipelines, diverters and a walkway; the off-spec silo is adjacent, with a truck bay for port rejects. Compressor house near the dense-phase vessels at the calciner base; aeration blower house at the silo base. The reclaim conveyor runs in a tunnel or ground-level gallery under the silo outlets to transfer tower TT-001. From there the overland conveyor follows a dedicated corridor to the port, shared with the caustic and fuel pipelines and power/fibre. Road access for the loadout is kept away from the main conveyor crossing points.
interfaces: A15 Calcination: product from FBC; off-spec return to P02 via the dust-return system
A17 Port: overland conveyor delivery to the port silos; port rejects returned by tanker to 16-SI-003; caustic and fuel pipelines share the corridor
A20 Utilities/layout: the overland conveyor (not rail) is the adopted refinery-to-port mode; compressed air, MV power, control system (despatch inventory)
Laboratory: product certificates from composite samples

areas.area_name: Port & export (alumina export; caustic, fuel and lime import)
areas.purpose: Receive SGA by overland conveyor, store ~100,000 t at the port, and load bulk carriers (Handysize to Panamax) at ~2,000 t/h with enclosed, dust-controlled handling and trade-certified weighing and sampling. Receive bulk liquid caustic soda (50 % NaOH) and fuel oil/diesel from tankers at a common-user liquid berth, and quicklime by ship at a multipurpose berth (or by road), for transfer to the refinery and mine. Keep alumina, caustic and oil out of the sea: enclosed galleries, spill trays, stormwater capture and marine spill response.
areas.process_description: EXPORT: 1) The overland conveyor discharges at the port receiving tower onto a 1,200 mm silo-top conveyor with plough/diverter gates into 4 x 25,000 t concrete silos (100,000 t, ~18 days, ~1.5-2 cargoes). A reject diverter in the receiving tower can send wet or contaminated alumina to a reject bin. 2) For ship loading, two silos are reclaimed together through aerated bottoms and flow-control gates onto a 1,600 mm reclaim conveyor. It feeds a ~300-500 t aerated surge bin in transfer tower TT-002, whose flow-control gate sets a steady rate onto the jetty conveyor. The jetty conveyor runs in an enclosed gallery with a closed floor and spill trays on a trestle. It feeds the wharf conveyor, whose tripper feeds the travelling shiploader. 3) A trade-certified belt weigher (OIML R50) and a primary cross-stream sampler (ISO 2927 principles) on the jetty conveyor give the shipping weight and the quality-certificate sample, and draft surveys confirm the weight. 4) The rail-mounted, luffing and telescopic (shuttle) shiploader moves between hatches. Its telescopic cascade chute with dust extraction places the alumina low in the hold to reduce dust and aeration. Holds must be clean and dry. Alumina (IMSBC Code group C) flows freely when aerated and must be trimmed. No water sprays are used on the product (moisture spec): dust control is by enclosure and bag filters. 5) Typical vessels are Handysize/Supramax of 25,000-60,000 DWT (cargo ~30,000-55,000 t), with Panamax of 65,000-80,000 DWT as the design vessel (laden draft up to ~14.5 m); ~40-60 shipments/yr. A loading rate of ~2,000 t/h rated (~1,400-1,700 t/h effective, including hatch changes) loads a 50,000 t cargo in ~30-40 h. 6) Port reject alumina (spillage, rain-wetted or contaminated material) is collected in a reject bin and trucked back to the refinery off-spec silo. All alumina-handling areas drain to stormwater capture sumps and a sedimentation/first-flush pond, with no direct discharge to sea. IMPORT: 7) Caustic soda 50 % w/w (UN 1824, class 8) arrives in chemical tankers (parcels of ~15,000-25,000 t of solution) at a common-user liquid berth. Ship pumps discharge at ~300-600 m3/h through a DN 250 loading arm (hose backup) to 2 x ~15,000 m3 carbon-steel tanks (API 650), held below ~45-50 degC (caustic SCC limit, NACE SP0403). Transfer pumps send caustic in batches (~100-120 m3/h, ~5-7 h/d) through a DN 200 pipeline in the conveyor corridor to refinery caustic storage. 8) Fuel oil (HFO: backup/alternative calciner and boiler fuel) and diesel (mine fleet) are received the same way through a DN 300 arm into heated (HFO) and plain bunded tanks. 9) Quicklime (IMSBC 'LIME (UNSLAKED)', group B: reacts with water and releases heat) is ~60,000-100,000 t/yr (design ~90,000 t/yr). It arrives either by road from a regional lime kiln or as bulk carrier parcels unloaded at the multipurpose berth by a mobile harbour crane into a dust-controlled eco-hopper, then covered or pneumatic trucks to the refinery lime silos.

streams.from_to: Bulk carrier -> 17-MC-001 grab -> 17-HP-001 -> trucks -> refinery lime silos
streams.basis: CHANGED to align with A20 (~89 kt/yr; ~40 kg CaO/t Al2O3)

equipment.name: Port receiving tower, reject diverter and silo-top distribution conveyor
equipment.function: Receive the overland conveyor, divert reject material, and distribute alumina into any port silo.
equipment.type_selected: Enclosed troughed belt conveyor (1,200 mm) across the silo roofs with pneumatic plough/diverter-gate discharge points
equipment.why_this_type: Simple, enclosed and able to feed any selected silo.
key_dimensions: Belt 1,200 mm (CORRECTED from 1,050 mm for ~55-60 % fill); length ~150-200 m across 4 silos at ~60-70 m elevation (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: An inclined gallery lifts the belt to the silo roofs. Plough or diverter gates over each silo inlet send the stream into the selected silo. A flap diverter in the receiving tower can send wet or contaminated material to the reject bin instead. A dust collector serves each discharge point.
details_to_model: Inclined truss gallery with cladding and walkways both sides; receiving tower with chutes, reject flap diverter and dust collector; plough diverters with actuators above each silo inlet
hazards_and_safety: Work at height; conveyor guarding; wind exposure

equipment.name: Port alumina storage silos with aeration blowers
equipment.function: Store ~100,000 t SGA to assemble ship cargoes and buffer shipping delays.
equipment.type_selected: Slip-formed concrete silos with aerated multi-sector floors and central cones (same technology as 16-SI)
equipment.why_this_type: Silos give weather-proof storage free of contamination and reclaim at a high rate by gravity and aeration, without mobile equipment. Large enclosed sheds with portal reclaimers (used at some alumina ports) are the alternative, but they need mobile equipment and make more dust.
key_dimensions: ID ~28-30 m; wall ~45-50 m; overall ~55-65 m (engineering estimate: 25,000 t at ~1.0 t/m3)
Silo spacing ~5-10 m; common stair/lift tower

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate (~1.3-2 x largest typical cargo)

equipment.working_principle: These work the same way as the refinery silos. Sequential sector aeration fluidises the alumina above the active sectors, and it flows through the central-cone outlets and flow-control gates into airslides and onto the reclaim conveyor. The silo gates are trimmed to hold the surge bin level, while the surge bin gate holds the shiploader rate steady.
details_to_model: Four tall concrete cylinders in a row; roof house with distribution conveyor, vent filters and inlets
Base outlet chambers with gates and airslides; blower house with rotary-lobe blowers; reclaim tunnel below
Radar level, P/V relief, lightning protection, aircraft lighting if required, cyclone-rated design for coastal sites
hazards_and_safety: Engulfment / drowning in fluidised material; confined space; work at height
Coastal wind loads; corrosion protection

equipment.name: Shiploading surge bin with flow-control gate (in transfer tower TT-002)
equipment.function: Holds a steady loading rate during silo changeover and gate adjustments, and gives the trade weigher a steady feed.
equipment.qty_standby: 0 (bypass chute around the bin for maintenance at reduced rate)
equipment.type_selected: Steel bin with aerated cone bottom, twin pneumatic flow-control gates and load cells
equipment.why_this_type: Aerated silo gates respond slowly and switching silos causes rate swings. A small live buffer separates silo reclaim from the jetty conveyor. Partly accepted: the belt weigher is accurate across its rated range anyway, so the main benefit is a steady rate and fewer trips on overload or underload.
key_dimensions: Live capacity ~300-500 t (~9-15 min at 2,000 t/h); ~8-9 m dia x ~10-12 m cylinder + cone (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: The reclaim conveyor fills the bin from the top. The bin sits on load cells, and aeration pads in its cone keep the alumina fluid at the outlets. The outlet flow-control gate is driven by the rate set point from the shiploader operator. The silo gates are adjusted to hold the bin weight in its control band. A vent filter on the roof handles the displaced air.
details_to_model: Cylindrical bin inside the transfer tower framing; roof inlet chute and vent filter
Aerated cone with 2 outlets, slide gates + pneumatic flow-control gates, short airslides/chutes to the jetty conveyor loading point
Load cells under the support ring, radar level, inspection doors, bypass chute with flap gate
hazards_and_safety: Confined space and engulfment; aeration and gates locked out before entry
Work at height in the tower
sources: Claudius Peters / IBAU bin and flow-gate practice

equipment.name: Reclaim, jetty and wharf conveyors with trade belt weigher and shipment sampler
equipment.function: Convey alumina from the port silos along the jetty to the shiploader, weigh the cargo for trade, and take the quality-certificate sample.
equipment.qty_operating: 3 conveyors in series (reclaim, jetty, wharf with tripper)
equipment.type_selected: Enclosed troughed belt conveyors 1,600 mm at ~4.0 m/s; jetty conveyor in a closed gallery with solid floor plate and spill trays on a piled trestle; OIML R50 class 0.5 belt scale; cross-stream primary sampler with sample preparation
equipment.why_this_type: A high rate with full enclosure and spill containment over water, so nothing spills to sea.
key_dimensions: Belt 1,600 mm at ~4.0 m/s (CORRECTED from 1,400 mm): required area 2,200/(0.95 x 3,600 x 4.0) = ~0.16 m2 vs ~0.25-0.26 m2 for 1,600 mm, 35 deg trough, 10 deg surcharge = ~60-65 % fill
Jetty length site-specific, ~0.5-2 km (engineering estimate)
Drives ~250-630 kW each (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Belt conveyors carry the alumina from the silos to the wharf. On the wharf conveyor, a travelling tripper (part of the shiploader) lifts the belt over a pair of pulleys and discharges onto the shiploader boom belt, wherever the loader stands. The trade belt weigher totals the mass and is calibrated with test chains and by a material test against a weighbridge. The sampler cuts the full stream at fixed intervals to build a composite for ISO testing. Any spillage or belt-cleaner carry-back over the water drops onto the closed gallery floor or spill trays, never into the sea.
details_to_model: Fully clad jetty gallery with closed floor plate, walkway, windows, lighting and fire detection; continuous spill trays under carry and return strands draining to land-side sumps
Trestle on steel piles with cross-bracing
Wharf conveyor along the berth in a covered trench with rails for the belt-lifting tripper carriage
Trade weigher in a wind-shielded section; sampler house with cutter, secondary divider and sample bottles
Transfer towers with dust collectors; pull-wires, drift switches
hazards_and_safety: Conveyor entrapment; falls over water (life rings, rescue boat access)
Lightning/wind on exposed galleries
sources: OIML R50 continuous totalising automatic weighing instruments

equipment.name: Port reject / off-spec alumina bin with truck loadout
equipment.function: Segregates rain-wetted, contaminated or spilled alumina at the port and loads it for return to the refinery off-spec silo.
equipment.type_selected: Steel bin with aerated cone, telescopic dustless loading spout to pressure-discharge road tankers (covered skip bins for wet clean-up material)
equipment.why_this_type: Off-spec material must not reach a ship. The refinery off-spec silo (16-SI-003) is the only reprocessing route, so the port needs a segregated hold point and a transport link.
key_dimensions: ~200-300 t; ~6-7 m dia x ~8-10 m + cone, on legs with ~5 m truck clearance (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: The reject diverter in the receiving tower, or vacuum-truck and loader clean-up, delivers material to the bin. When a tanker load has built up, it is loaded through the dust-extracted spout. The tanker then blows it into the refinery off-spec silo, where it is reprocessed slowly. Wet lumps go by covered skip to digestion or disposal as the refinery chemist decides.
details_to_model: Bin on four legs over a truck lane, vent filter on roof, aerated cone, slide gate, telescopic loading spout, weighbridge, skip-bin bay for wet clean-up material
hazards_and_safety: Confined space; vehicle movements; work at height on tanker roofs (fall-arrest gantry)

equipment.name: Travelling shiploader (rail-mounted, luffing and telescopic boom)
equipment.function: Loads alumina into bulk carriers at ~2,000 t/h, reaching every hatch and across the full ship's beam.
equipment.qty_standby: 0 (port silo buffer; maintenance windows between ships)
equipment.type_selected: Rail-mounted travelling shiploader with luffing boom, telescopic (shuttle) boom conveyor, tripper, and telescopic cascade loading chute with dust extraction
equipment.why_this_type: One loader on a straight wharf covers Handysize to Panamax vessels. Luffing clears the ship's air draft, and the shuttle reaches the far side of the hold without warping the ship along the berth.
key_dimensions: Rail gauge ~12-16 m; travel length ~220-260 m (engineering estimate)
Outreach from fender line: max ~31-33 m (shuttle extended), min ~10 m (CORRECTED per review for Panamax beam 32.3 m + ~2-3 m fender standoff)
Shuttle stroke ~15-20 m, luff angle ~-10 to +15 deg (engineering estimate)
Boom belt 1,600 mm; loader mass ~700-1,300 t (engineering estimate)
Clearance under boom ~18-22 m above wharf (site/tide dependent, engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: engineering estimate; design per AS 4324.1 / ISO 5049-1

equipment.working_principle: The loader travels on two rails along the wharf. The wharf conveyor belt passes through the tripper carriage, which raises the belt and discharges onto the loader's boom conveyor. The boom luffs (raised or lowered by hydraulic cylinders or a wire-rope winch) to clear hatch coamings and ship cranes. The boom conveyor shuttles in and out to place the chute anywhere across the hatch, out to the far coaming of a Panamax. The telescopic cascade chute drops the alumina through a series of cones, so it stays a dense stream instead of spreading as a plume. Its lower end sits close to the cargo pile, where an extraction ring draws dust back to the loader's bag filter. The operator in the boom cab follows a hatch sequence (load plan) to keep the ship's stresses and trim within limits.
details_to_model: Portal gantry (2 legs seaside, 2 landside) with equalised bogies (~16-32 wheels total), rail clamps, storm tie-down pins and pits, buffers
Tripper car coupled on the landside with inclined belt, discharge chute and dust seal
No slewing; luffing boom (box girder or truss) pivoted on the portal, with luffing cylinders/rope reeving and counterweight
Shuttle (telescopic) boom with 1,600 mm conveyor, belt covers, walkways and handrails both sides
Operator cab under/on the boom with tilted glazing and A/C; electrical house on the portal; MV cable reel and cable trench; anemometer at the boom tip
Telescopic cascade chute (~10-20 m extension) with hoist winch and dust extraction hood/skirt; trimming spoon optional
Anti-collision sensors (laser/radar) boom-to-ship and loader-to-obstacle, travel warning horns/beacons, emergency stops, lighting masts
Onboard pulse-jet dust collector at the boom tail transfer
hazards_and_safety: Boom/ship collision; crushing at the rails (travel alarms, wheel guards)
Wind and cyclone: automatic storm brakes, tie-downs, anemometer interlocks
Work at height and over water; hatch access (falls into holds), oxygen-depleted holds (entry permits)
Dust exposure at the hatch; noise
common_problems: Chute wear and liner replacement; dust at hatch openings when the chute is lifted high
Cable reel faults
operating_tips_and_key_points: Keep the chute discharge low in the pile; reduce rate when topping off to avoid alumina flushing
Agree the load plan with the ship's officer for trim and ballast; draft surveys at start and finish
instrumentation_and_control: PLC with position encoders (travel, luff, shuttle), load-plan display, rate set point to the surge-bin gate
Wind speed interlocks, overload/slack rope, end limits
equipment.materials: Structural steel (marine coating system ISO 12944 C5-M/CX)
sources: AS 4324.1 / ISO 5049-1 mobile equipment for continuous handling of bulk materials

equipment.name: Alumina export berth (wharf, fenders, mooring)
equipment.function: Berth and moor Handysize to Panamax bulk carriers safely alongside the shiploader.
equipment.type_selected: Open piled wharf (steel/concrete piles, concrete deck) or jetty head with mooring/breasting dolphins
equipment.why_this_type: Open piled structures suit deep-water, exposed sites and keep dredging to a minimum.
key_dimensions: Berth length ~250-280 m (engineering estimate; Panamax LOA ~225-230 m)

Dredged berth pocket ~-15.5 to -16 m CD for a laden Panamax (draft <=14.5 m + ~10 % UKC), or ~-13.5 to -14 m CD if the design vessel is limited to Supramax (draft ~12.5-13 m) (CORRECTED per review; engineering estimate, PIANC UKC guidance)
Deck level ~+4 to +6 m CD (site tide dependent)
equipment.working_principle: Fenders absorb the berthing energy. Mooring lines run from the ship to quick-release hooks (QRH) or bollards. Line tensions and environmental loads are checked against OCIMF MEG4 practice and the BS 6349 / PIANC design rules. Dense SGA cargoes load ships down to their marks, so the berth pocket depth is set by the laden draft of the design vessel plus under-keel clearance.
details_to_model: Cone or cell fenders with steel frontal panels at ~15-25 m spacing
Quick-release mooring hooks (100-150 t SWL) with remote release on mooring dolphins with access walkways
Shiploader rails with cable trench, wharf conveyor, rail stops
Gangway tower; bollards; ladders and life-rings at ~30 m; navigation lights; fire monitors and hydrants
Spill containment kerbs and deck drainage to land-side collection sumps
hazards_and_safety: Mooring line snap-back: treat the whole mooring area on the wharf and dolphins as a snap-back danger zone (OCIMF MEG4). Keep people out during line tensioning and let-go, use QRH remote release, and limit access to essential line handlers standing out of line of the bight. Do not rely on painted zones (CORRECTED per review)
Falls into water; ship movement
Heavy vehicles on the wharf deck
sources: PIANC WG 33 / WG 145 (fenders, berthing); PIANC UKC guidance
OCIMF Mooring Equipment Guidelines 4th ed. (MEG4, 2018) - snap-back clause to be confirmed

equipment.name: Common-user liquid berth (caustic, HFO, diesel) with manifold platform
equipment.function: Berth chemical/product tankers for caustic soda, fuel oil and diesel discharge.
equipment.type_selected: Jetty head (loading platform) with breasting and mooring dolphins linked by catwalks, connected to shore by a pipe trestle
equipment.why_this_type: A compact jetty head carries only the arms, manifold and fire protection, and the dolphins take the berthing and mooring loads. This is standard practice for small tankers and keeps hazardous liquids away from the alumina berth.
key_dimensions: Platform ~25-35 m x 15-20 m; 2-4 breasting + 4-6 mooring dolphins over ~150-200 m (engineering estimate for 10,000-30,000 DWT tankers, LOA ~120-180 m)
Berth pocket ~-11 to -12 m CD (engineering estimate)
Separation from alumina berth >=~150-300 m or per terminal risk assessment (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Tankers berth against the breasting dolphins and moor to the mooring dolphins with quick-release hooks. The ship's pumps discharge through the loading arms into shore pipelines. The manifold platform is kerbed and drains to a closed sump, so drips and spills cannot reach the sea.
details_to_model: Concrete jetty head on raked steel piles; kerbed, drained manifold area with drip trays and sump
Breasting dolphins with cone fenders; mooring dolphins with QRHs; steel catwalks with handrails
Pipe trestle to shore carrying the caustic (DN 250), HFO/diesel (DN 300) lines, fire main and power
Fire monitors (foam/water), safety showers and eyewash at the caustic arm, gangway, life-rings, lighting, ESD push-buttons
hazards_and_safety: Caustic spray; fuel fire; mooring snap-back (whole mooring area treated as a danger zone per MEG4)
Falls into water

equipment.name: Multipurpose berth and marine spill-response equipment
equipment.function: Berth general cargo/lime vessels for the mobile harbour crane, and store the terminal's marine spill-response kit.
equipment.type_selected: Solid or piled quay with paved apron; Tier-1 oil spill response kit (containment booms, skimmers, temporary storage, sorbents) and a workboat
equipment.why_this_type: Lime parcels and project cargo need a crane-served apron. Tankers discharging oil need a Tier-1 response on site, as port and licence conditions require. Caustic spills cannot be boomed, because the caustic dissolves, so prevention (PERCs, drip trays, kerbed manifolds) is the main control for caustic.
key_dimensions: Berth ~180-200 m, pocket ~-11 to -12 m CD (Handysize) (engineering estimate)
Boom length ~1.5 x LOA of largest tanker (~300-400 m) on reels; skimmer ~20-50 m3/h; workboat ~8-12 m (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.unit: kPa (mobile crane outrigger pads on spreader plates)

equipment.working_principle: The mobile harbour crane works from the apron with outriggers on load-spreading pads. During every oil transfer the spill kit and workboat are on standby. On an oil release the boom is deployed round the source, and the skimmer recovers oil to temporary tanks.
details_to_model: Concrete apron with crane pad markings, bollards, fenders, kerbs and drainage to oily-water separator
Spill-response shed with boom reels, skimmers, power packs, IBC storage, slipway or davit for the workboat
hazards_and_safety: Suspended loads; vehicle movements; falls into water; boat operations
sources: IMO OPRC Convention; national port spill-response plans

equipment.name: Port dust collection system (transfer towers, silo roofs, surge bin, shiploader)
equipment.function: Capture alumina dust at all transfer points, bins and the loading chute.
equipment.type_selected: Pulse-jet bag filters with fans
equipment.why_this_type: Water sprays are not acceptable on SGA (moisture/MOI spec), and dry filtration recovers product.
key_dimensions: ~100-800 m2 cloth each (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: These work as 16-DC does. Each enclosure is held at a slight negative pressure, so dust is drawn into the filter instead of escaping.
details_to_model: Filter casings with hoppers, rotary valves returning dust to the belt, fans and short stacks, extraction hoods at chutes
hazards_and_safety: Confined space, compressed air, work at height
sources: EU JRC BREF NFM 2017 / BREF on Emissions from Storage

equipment.name: Port stormwater / alumina capture sumps and sedimentation (first-flush) pond
equipment.function: Collect runoff, wash-down water and spillage from the alumina, caustic and fuel areas, so that nothing is discharged untreated to sea.
equipment.type_selected: Concrete sumps with submersible or vertical sump pumps; lined sedimentation/first-flush pond with outlet weir, pH monitoring and controlled discharge or reuse; separate oily-water separator for the fuel areas
equipment.why_this_type: Alumina is fine and drains easily into the sea. Caustic raises pH and oil forms a sheen. Licences at alumina export terminals require capture and treatment.
key_dimensions: Sumps ~3 x 3 x 3 m; pond sized for first-flush of ~15-25 mm runoff over the terminal paved area (engineering estimate, local rainfall governs)
equipment.working_principle: Kerbed slabs, gallery spill trays and bund drains send all water to the sumps. The sump pumps lift it to the pond, where the alumina settles. Settled water is reused for wash-down or discharged under licence after pH correction. Settled alumina is dug out periodically and sent back through the reject route.
details_to_model: Grated sumps with pump mounting plates, level controls, discharge pipes to the pond
Lined pond with inlet energy dissipator, outlet weir box, pH/turbidity analyser, discharge valve, access ramp for clean-out
Oily-water separator package near the tank farm
hazards_and_safety: Drowning in pond/sumps (fencing, life-rings); caustic contamination of water; confined-space entry to sumps

equipment.name: Marine loading arms / hose system for caustic and fuel import
equipment.function: Connect tanker manifolds to the shore pipelines for caustic soda and fuel oil/diesel discharge.
equipment.qty_operating: 1 caustic arm (DN 250), 1 fuel arm (DN 300) at the common-user liquid berth
equipment.type_selected: Counterbalanced marine loading arms with powered emergency release couplers (PERC)
equipment.why_this_type: Safe, repeatable connections for hazardous liquids. The PERC prevents a rupture if the ship drifts.
key_dimensions: Caustic arm DN 250 (10 in); fuel arm DN 300 (12 in) (CORRECTED from DN 200-250 to keep velocity <=~3.5 m/s)
Arm reach envelope ~15-20 m; riser ~10-15 m (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: Articulated pipe arms with swivel joints, balanced by counterweights, connect to the ship's manifold through a quick-connect coupler. If the ship moves beyond the operating envelope, the PERC closes valves on both sides and separates, so very little spills.
details_to_model: Riser, inner arm, outer arm, counterweight, swivels, quick-connect/disconnect coupler, PERC with double ball valves, hydraulic power pack, drip tray
Caustic arm (stainless or CS, colour-coded) kept separate from the fuel arm; insulating flange for electrical isolation of the ship
hazards_and_safety: Caustic spray (severe burns/blindness): face shield, chemical suit, safety showers on the berth
Fuel fire, static discharge; spill to sea (booms on standby for oil)
sources: OCIMF Design and Construction Specification for Marine Loading Arms

equipment.name: Caustic soda (50 % NaOH) import storage tanks
equipment.function: Store imported caustic soda for transfer to the refinery.
equipment.type_selected: Vertical fixed cone-roof carbon-steel tanks (API 650) in a concrete bund, insulated (and heated only where ambient falls below ~15 degC)
equipment.why_this_type: Carbon steel is acceptable for 50 % NaOH below the caustic stress-corrosion-cracking limit (keep below ~45-50 degC without PWHT, per the NACE SP0403 chart).
key_dimensions: ~15,000 m3 each: ~32-34 m dia x ~18-20 m high (engineering estimate)
Bund capacity >=110 % of largest tank (AS 3780 / local codes)

operating_parameters.basis: NACE SP0403 limits; crystallisation ~12 degC for 50 %

equipment.working_principle: These are atmospheric storage tanks, filled from ship discharge and emptied by the transfer pumps. A breather vent, optionally with a CO2 scrubber, limits carbonation. High-level alarms and an independent high-high trip that closes the ship-discharge valve prevent overfill.
details_to_model: Cylindrical tank with external spiral stair, roof handrail, roof manhole, breather vent
Shell manways (2), inlet nozzle with internal downcomer, outlet nozzle with ROSOV, drain, sample point
Radar level gauge + independent high-high level switch; temperature element
Insulation (where used) with metal cladding; steam/electric heating coil (where required)
Concrete bund wall with sump and pump; safety showers/eyewash at bund access and pump area; corrosive signage
hazards_and_safety: Caustic burns and eye damage; slippery spills; never mix with acids or aluminium (H2 generation)
Confined-space entry only after neutralisation and gas test (H2 possible if aluminium was present)
sources: AS 3780 Storage and handling of corrosive substances

equipment.name: Caustic transfer pumps and pipeline to refinery
equipment.function: Pump caustic in batches from the port tanks to refinery caustic storage.
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal centrifugal pumps (ISO 5199 / API 610 OH2) with double mechanical seals; carbon-steel welded pipeline DN 200 with leak detection and pigging/flushing facilities
equipment.why_this_type: Reliable batch transfer, with double seals to stop caustic leaks. DN 200 keeps friction moderate for viscous 50 % caustic (~15-30 cP at 40-50 degC).
key_dimensions: Pump ~100-120 m3/h at ~90-130 m head, 75-110 kW (engineering estimate)
Pipeline ~8 km DN 200 (CORRECTED: DN 150 at this flow would need ~200 m friction head); design pressure ~25 bar(g) (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: The centrifugal pump raises the pressure to overcome pipeline friction and static head. Refinery tank level sets when batches start and stop, and a control valve or VFD sets the rate. A mass-balance leak detection system compares the meters at each end and alarms on any loss. Where ambient can fall below ~15 degC, the line is buried or heat-traced, and it is flushed with water or weak liquor before long shutdowns so that caustic cannot crystallise in it.
details_to_model: Pump sets in a bunded pump bay with seal pots (barrier fluid), suction/discharge valves, strainers, gauges, splash guards over flanges
Pipeline on sleepers in the conveyor corridor (or buried) with marker posts, flush connections, block valves, flow meters at each end
hazards_and_safety: Caustic spray from flanges/seals (flange guards), burns; safety showers

equipment.name: Fuel oil (HFO) and diesel import tanks and transfer pumps
equipment.function: Store HFO (backup/alternative calciner and boiler fuel) and diesel (mine fleet), and transfer them to the refinery and mine.
equipment.type_selected: API 650 cone-roof tanks for HFO (heated and insulated) and internal floating-roof tank for diesel, in bunds; positive-displacement screw pumps for HFO
equipment.why_this_type: HFO must be heated to stay pumpable, and screw pumps handle viscous oil.
key_dimensions: HFO ~10,000-15,000 m3 each; diesel ~3,000-5,000 m3 (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: The tanks are filled from tankers through the fuel loading arm. Heating coils (steam or thermal oil) keep the HFO viscosity low enough to pump. Screw pumps send fuel by pipeline to the refinery, and diesel goes by road tanker to the mine.
details_to_model: Insulated HFO tanks with heater-coil nozzles, suction heaters, foam pourers, fixed fire-water cooling rings
Bunds, oily-water separator, truck loading bay
Screw pump sets with strainers and relief valves
hazards_and_safety: Fire/explosion (NFPA 30 / AS 1940), H2S in HFO tank headspace, hot oil burns, spill to sea

equipment.name: Mobile harbour crane with grab and dust-controlled eco-hopper (quicklime import)
equipment.function: Unload bulk quicklime (and general cargo/spares) from vessels at the multipurpose berth.
equipment.type_selected: Rubber-tyred mobile harbour crane (~100-150 t class) with electro-hydraulic clamshell grab; mobile eco-hopper with bag filter and flap-sealed grid
equipment.why_this_type: Flexible for small, irregular import parcels. The eco-hopper contains the highly irritant lime dust.
key_dimensions: Grab ~10-20 m3; hopper ~40-60 m3 on legs high enough for trucks to load underneath (~5 m clearance) (engineering estimate)

operating_parameters.basis: CHANGED to align with A20 (~89 kt/yr)

equipment.working_principle: The crane grabs lime from the hold and opens the grab over the hopper grid. Self-closing flaps and an extraction filter keep the dust inside the hopper. Lime discharges into covered tippers or pneumatic tankers below, which haul it to the refinery lime silos.
details_to_model: Crane on outriggers with tower, boom, cab and grab; eco-hopper with filter house, fan, discharge gate, truck lane, wheel-wash
hazards_and_safety: Quicklime reacts exothermically with water: keep it dry and never fight a fire in bulk lime with water; burns to eyes, skin and lungs (full PPE and RPE)
Suspended loads; vehicle movements

equipment.name: Port fire water pumps (electric, diesel, jockey)
equipment.function: Provide fire water and foam for the berths, tank farm and conveyors.
equipment.type_selected: Horizontal split-case fire pumps per NFPA 20, with diesel-driven standby
equipment.why_this_type: Code-listed fire pumps give a reliable supply that does not depend on grid power.
key_dimensions: ~500-1,000 m3/h at ~100-120 m head (engineering estimate)
equipment.working_principle: The jockey pump keeps the ring main pressurised. When a hydrant or monitor opens and the pressure falls, the duty pump starts automatically. The diesel pump starts if the duty pump fails or power is lost.
details_to_model: Pump house with split-case pumps, diesel engine with fuel tank and exhaust, controllers, test header, fire water tank
hazards_and_safety: Rotating equipment; diesel fuel

areas.layout_notes: The port terminal sits on reclaimed or natural land behind the berths. Four alumina silos stand in a row ~200-500 m from the wharf, with the receiving tower (and reject bin) at the overland conveyor end. The reclaim tunnel under the silos leads to transfer tower TT-002 with the surge bin. From there the enclosed jetty gallery runs on a piled trestle (length site-specific) to a single alumina berth ~250-280 m long, dredged to ~-15.5 to -16 m CD for laden Panamax. The shiploader rails run the full berth length, with storm tie-down points at a parking position at one end. The common-user liquid berth (17-WH-002) is a separate jetty head ~150-300 m from the alumina berth. The caustic and fuel tank farm sits in a separate bunded compound >= ~50-100 m from the alumina silos and conveyors (spill and fire separation), connected to the liquid berth by a pipe trestle. The caustic (DN 200) and fuel lines to the refinery follow the overland conveyor corridor. The multipurpose berth (17-WH-003) with mobile harbour crane, eco-hopper and spill-response store lies at the far end from the alumina berth. Stormwater sumps sit at the low points of each area, with the first-flush pond at the terminal low point away from the berths. Also on site: substation/e-house, a control room with a view of the berths, workshop, laboratory sample room, and gatehouse with truck weighbridge. All structures use marine corrosion protection (ISO 12944 C5-M/CX) and are designed for cyclonic wind where it applies (e.g., Indian East Coast, northern Australia).

Calciner count and outage strategy: 2 x 3,500 t/d with ~4-5 days of hydrate slurry storage (15-TK-001/002) vs 3 x 2,300-2,500 t/d. A13/A14 owners to accept the storage tie-ins and ~110-120 % product-filter capacity, and to agree the production cut-back plan for 2-3 week refractory relines.

Refinery-to-port: the ~8 km covered overland conveyor (coastal refinery) is now the adopted basis. A20 must remove its 30-60 km rail assumption and A19 its rail/road caustic bays. If the SMEs instead want an inland refinery, A16/A17 must be redesigned with rail loadout/unloading and pressure-discharge or covered hopper wagons.
Port storage form: silos chosen (4 x 25,000 t). Some alumina ports use large enclosed sheds with portal/bridge reclaimers; confirm SME preference and port land availability.

Port location and vessel mix: confirm channel depth, tidal range and maximum vessel. Panamax sets the berth pocket at ~-15.5 to -16 m CD, shiploader outreach at ~31-33 m and port storage; a Supramax limit allows ~-13.5 to -14 m CD.

Emission limits: confirm the jurisdiction (e.g., India CPCB/SPCB vs Western Australia DWER licence) for particulate (30 vs 50 mg/Nm3), NOx and stack height, plus port stormwater discharge limits (pH, TSS).
FBC heat recovery: confirm whether the recovered heat (~4-8 MW per train) goes to hydrate wash water (assumed), spent liquor heating, or a cooling tower only.
Caustic consumption and lime demand to be finally reconciled with the A05/A08/A19 owners. Current basis: ~150 kt/yr NaOH and ~90 kt/yr quicklime; lime supply by road vs ship to be decided.

Caustic pipeline climate: if the generic site has winter ambient below ~15 degC (e.g., southern WA), the DN 200 caustic line needs burial or heat tracing and a flushing procedure; confirm site climate.
